sections.heading: How do you check that a tutor really knows your child's syllabus?
paragraphs: Ask them to name the papers your child will sit, and the code of the specification. A tutor who has taught that course answers in one sentence. A tutor who has not will answer with the subject name, and I teach IGCSE is not an adequate answer to this question.

Before anyone reaches your shortlist we check identity against government photo identification, the degrees and teaching qualifications they claim, and a teaching history that can be followed up. We ask which specifications they have taught, for how long, and when they last prepared a student for that board's papers. Every IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai on a shortlist has been through the same checks, and their answers reach you in their own words rather than as ticks in a grid, because the phrasing tells you things a checkbox never will.

Your own checks take about ten minutes on the first call. Ask which awarding body. Ask for the code. Ask how many papers the subject has and what each one is for. Ask what the tutor would bring to a first session at your home. Then ask about one specific thing from the unit your child is on this fortnight, and listen for whether the answer is about this course or about the subject in the abstract. The difference is audible.

The answers that should slow you down are the vague ones. A tutor who says the boards are basically the same, or who offers a thick folder of past papers without first checking which board they came from, has told you how the term will go. There is no single home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families study, and anyone presenting themselves that way deserves a second question rather than a booking. None of this is about catching people out. Strong tutors welcome these questions, because they are the questions that let them show preparation they have already done.
bullets: Identity, qualifications and teaching history are checked before a shortlist is sent.
Ask every candidate for the awarding body and the syllabus code.
Ask how many papers the subject has and what each assesses.
Treat the boards are basically the same as a warning, not reassurance.
Ask what the tutor will bring to the first session at your table.

sections.heading: The specification document your family has probably never opened
paragraphs: Every IGCSE subject has a specification, and it is public. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel both publish theirs on their own websites, free, as a document anyone can download in under a minute. It runs to a few dozen pages, it is written in plain administrative English rather than in jargon, and almost nobody in Mumbai has opened the one that governs their child's year. It is the most useful document in this entire process and it costs nothing at all.

It tells you what the course actually is. The content list says which topics are examinable and, by omission, which are not, which settles a surprising number of arguments at the dining table. The assessment section names the components, says what each is for and how long it lasts. The assessment objectives describe what examiners are rewarding, which is not always what a student assumes. There is normally a section on command words, the vocabulary the questions themselves are written in, and a note on permitted equipment or reference material. Where a subject offers routes or options, the specification is where that is laid out plainly.

Now set that beside the failure this page exists to prevent. A tutor arrives with a folder of past papers accumulated over years, picks one and works through it for an hour. If that paper belongs to the other awarding body, your child has spent the hour on a question structure they will not meet, in wording their examiner does not use, and occasionally on content sitting outside their own list. The hour is not wasted in the sense that the subject is still the subject. It is wasted in the sense that it was sold as exam practice and it was not exam practice.

You can hear the difference inside one session. A tutor who has read your child's specification refers to components by name, knows which command word a question is testing, and can explain why one past question is worth attempting now and another is not. A tutor who has not read it talks about the subject. Both may know the material equally well. Only one of them is teaching the course your child is entered for, and that distinction is the entire argument of this page.
bullets: Specifications are published free by each awarding body as a downloadable document.
The content list tells you what is examinable and what is not.
Command words are the vocabulary your child's exam questions are written in.
Papers from the wrong board teach a structure your child will not meet.
Ask your tutor which specification version they read and when.

sections.heading: What should progress look like after four weeks with the right board?
paragraphs: After four weeks, expect fluency rather than grades. Your child should be able to say which board they are entered with, name the papers, and recognise the command words in a question. Marks move later than that. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and anybody who does is selling you something other than teaching.

Over a full term the signal changes shape. Work comes back with fewer structural errors rather than simply fewer arithmetic slips. Your child begins using the board's own language without being prompted to. A school assessment that previously produced half a blank page produces an attempt, even an imperfect one. Questions at home become more specific, which is usually the clearest sign of all. If none of that is visible by the end of a term, the problem deserves to be named out loud rather than parked until the next report card arrives.

Across a whole exam cycle the honest position is that a tutor is one input among several, and the others are the school, the work the student does alone, and a run of weeks nobody controls. A tutor teaching the correct specification removes one category of avoidable loss, which is genuinely worth having and is not the same thing as a promised outcome. There are no guarantees here. A tutor who offers one has told you how much care they take with everything else they say.

If it is not working, say so in week three rather than week ten. Tell us what you are actually seeing: the sessions run but nothing is ever set, the tutor is pleasant and the folder never changes, your child starts dreading the slot. We ask the tutor for their version, because sometimes the repair is a changed time or a sharper brief rather than a changed person. Where the match is genuinely wrong we replace it, and a replacement is a fresh shortlist on the same brief with everything the first attempt taught you folded into it.
bullets: Four weeks: your child can name the board, the code and the papers.
One term: structural errors fall and the board's language appears unprompted.
One exam cycle: a tutor is one input among school, effort and circumstance.
IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor will either.

sections.heading: Getting started with IGCSE home tutors in Mumbai
paragraphs: Send four things and the first conversation starts in the right place: the awarding body, the subject with its code if you have it, your child's school year, and your address with the evenings that genuinely work. If the code is not to hand, photograph the front cover and the spine of the set textbook and the most recent school report. That is usually enough for us to work out what needs confirming with the school before anyone is shortlisted.

We come back with a shortlist built on the board first and the subject second. You speak to every tutor on it yourself before anything is booked, and you ask them the questions set out on this page. The best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai for your child is not an abstract ranking. It is the person who has taught your child's specification, can reach your building on a weekday evening, and gets along with a fifteen year old who would rather be doing almost anything else.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel like it. The tutor confirms the specification, looks through recent school work, works a short piece of the current unit and watches how your child handles an unfamiliar question rather than a rehearsed one. At the end you should receive a plain statement of what they found and what the next four sessions will cover. If that does not arrive on its own, ask for it, and treat the quality of the answer as information.

Fees are agreed directly with the tutor. IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on the board and level, how scarce that subject specialism is, how far the tutor travels, and how long and how often each session runs, which is why any figure quoted before anyone has read the brief means very little. An IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai for a thinly taught subject is priced differently from one for a widely taught subject, and that is a question of supply rather than a statement about quality.
bullets: Send the board, subject, school year, address and workable evening slots.
No code to hand? Photograph the textbook cover and the latest report.
Speak to every shortlisted tutor before a first session is booked.
The first session is diagnostic and ends with a written plan.
Fees are agreed with the tutor, never quoted before the brief is read.

faqs.question: My child's school just says IGCSE. How do I find out which board?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer or the subject teacher directly, in writing, and ask for the awarding body and the syllabus code together. Three other sources corroborate it: the front cover and inside spine of the set textbook, which usually names the board and the course; the statement of entry, which lists the exact papers; and any past paper the school has already issued, which carries the board's name in its header. If two sources disagree, the statement of entry wins. This is the first thing we settle before shortlisting IGCSE home tutors in Mumbai, because every decision after it depends on the answer.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: They depend on five things, and none of them is a published rate card. The board and level, because a specialist in a thinly taught specification is harder to find. The subject itself, for the same reason. The travel distance, because an hour on the Western Express Highway is an hour the tutor is not teaching. The length and frequency of sessions. And whether the slot is at your home, online or a mix of both. Fees are agreed directly between you and the tutor, and we would rather explain the variables honestly than quote a number that will be wrong for your household.

faqs.question: A tutor told me they teach IGCSE. Is that enough to go ahead?
faqs.answer: No. I teach IGCSE describes a family of qualifications, not a course. Ask which awarding body, which syllabus code and which papers your child will sit, then listen for whether the reply is specific. A tutor who has taught that specification answers immediately and will usually volunteer something about the component structure without being pushed. A tutor who deflects back to the subject name is telling you they intend to teach the subject rather than the course. Both may be able teachers. Only one of them has read the document your child is being examined against.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who knows one board teach the other?
faqs.answer: Yes, with preparation, and you should ask what that preparation looks like. A strong subject teacher can move between awarding bodies, but only after reading the new specification properly, working through recent papers and mark schemes from that board, and understanding how its questions are worded. The honest version of this answer sounds like a plan with dates attached. The dishonest version is that the boards are basically the same. If a tutor is crossing over for your child, ask when they will have finished reading the specification and ask them to tell you afterwards what they found in it.

faqs.question: Will a tutor really travel to our building on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a sensible radius, and that radius is the thing to agree before you book rather than after. A Thane family on Ghodbunder Road and a South Mumbai family near Peddar Road face the same problem from opposite ends, because the evening peak roughly doubles an otherwise short trip. We match inside your zone wherever the board and subject allow it. Please clear gate access and a visitor pass in advance, and tell security the name beforehand, so a tutor is not standing at the desk for ten minutes of a sixty minute session.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during a home session?
faqs.answer: Someone should be at home, though they do not need to sit in on the lesson. Most families here want an adult present when a tutor is working with a teenager, and most tutors prefer it as well. Set up a table in a room with a door rather than the dining table beside the television, keep the phone in another room, and leave the textbook, the school diary and any returned assessment out before the tutor arrives. Ask for two minutes at the end of each session instead of a long monthly debrief, and you will know more than any report would tell you.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week three rather than week ten, and be specific about what you are observing. We ask the tutor for their account first, because sometimes the repair is a changed time, a clearer brief or a different room rather than a different person. Where the match is genuinely wrong we replace it, and the replacement runs on the same brief with whatever the first attempt taught you added into it. A mismatch is usually about pace, personality or the student's own engagement rather than about ability, and naming it early costs you nothing at all.

faqs.question: The only board specialist is far away. Is online as good as home tuition?
faqs.answer: For many students it is close, and for some subjects it is genuinely equivalent, but the answer depends on the child rather than on the technology. A fifteen year old who already works independently does well on a shared screen. One who needs someone beside them to slow the pace and insist on written working does better in the room. If the board specialist is in Kharghar and you are in Colaba, the usual recommendation is a hybrid week: online for the regular session and in person before an assessment. That beats a nearby tutor teaching the wrong specification.

faqs.question: What if my child's subjects are split across two boards?
faqs.answer: It happens, and it causes no trouble as long as everybody knows. Schools can enter different subjects with different awarding bodies, so a student may sit one board's papers in Mathematics and another board's in a science. Collect the code for each subject separately instead of assuming that one answer covers the whole timetable. When we shortlist, each subject is treated as its own brief, which in practice usually means two tutors rather than one. Tell each tutor about the other, because otherwise your child is the only person holding both halves of the picture.

faqs.question: How far ahead should the board question be settled?
faqs.answer: Before the first session, every time. This is not a question that needs lead time; it needs one email and a reply. The reason to settle it early is that the cost of being wrong grows steadily: a tutor working from the other board's material for a few weeks in Year 9 is a correctable detour, while the same mistake discovered close to the exam series is not. If you are starting part way through the year, confirm the board before you book anything, then let the tutor verify it in session one against your child's own work.

faqs.question: Will a board-specific tutor improve my child's result?
faqs.answer: No one can promise that, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades. What a tutor teaching the correct specification removes is a category of avoidable loss: hours spent on questions your child will never face, and surprise in the exam hall about the shape of a paper. That is worth having, and it is still not an outcome. The rest depends on the school, the work your child does between sessions, and things nobody controls. Any tutor who offers you a grade has just told you how carefully they choose their words.

sections.heading: How an IGCSE maths tutor in Mumbai gets matched
paragraphs: Most families who contact us about an IGCSE maths tutor in Mumbai arrive with a mark, not a diagnosis. The report says sixty-one percent and the teacher's comment says needs to show working. Our first job is turning that into something a tutor can act on: which tier the school has entered the child for, which syllabus route the school runs, whether the marks are being lost on topics the student has never understood or on questions they understood and rushed. Those two causes look identical on a report card and need completely different tuition.

So the form asks for the syllabus route if you know it, the grade or percentage from the last school assessment, the topics the teacher has flagged, and the evenings that are realistically free. Six to eight in the evening on a weekday is the slot every family in the city wants, which is why naming a second option changes your shortlist more than anything else you tell us. Maths tutors are the least scarce specialists in Mumbai and the strong ones are booked earliest, so a family that can take a Wednesday as well as a Thursday gets a better list in September than a family that can only take one night.

What you get back is a shortlist with teaching history, the tiers and routes each tutor has taught, and the areas they cover. No phone numbers go out until you pick someone. The trial session then runs on paper rather than conversation: the tutor sets a past-paper question in a topic the teacher flagged, watches the student attempt it without help, and marks it out loud so you can hear which marks were lost on method and which on arithmetic. Parents who sit in on that ten minutes usually know by the end whether to continue.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: which tier is your child on?
paragraphs: Your child sits one of two tiers in Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics, and the tier caps the range of grades available to them. Core covers a smaller syllabus and awards a restricted band of grades. Extended covers the full syllabus and the full grade range. The current syllabus document states exactly which grades each tier can award, and because boards revise those documents on their own schedule, the version for the year your child sits is the only one worth planning from. Your school's examinations officer holds it and will tell you which tier the entry has been made for.

Underneath the tier sits a second question most parents never hear about: which maths route the school runs at all. A Mathematics (0580) tutor in Mumbai teaches something different from a tutor working on Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics (0607), which expects a graphics calculator throughout and carries an investigation component. Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics (0606) runs alongside the main course for students heading towards demanding quantitative subjects. Pearson Edexcel runs its own International GCSE in Mathematics with Foundation and Higher tiers and separate specifications, plus Further Pure Mathematics. The header of your child's last mock paper carries the code that settles all of this in three seconds.

This page covers the breadth: the routes, the tiers, how to tell which one applies and how tuition differs across them. Mathematics (0580) at IGCSE Years 9-11 needs a tutor Mumbai parents can keep to one evening a week, and the code-level depth for that syllabus, paper by paper, lives on our Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 pages. If your child is in Year 7 or 8 and the question is Checkpoint rather than IGCSE, the Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint maths page is the right one. Sending you to the page that answers your actual question beats restating half of it here.

sections.heading: The non-calculator paper and the marks for method
paragraphs: Two things decide an Extended maths grade more than topic knowledge does, and both are trainable. The first is arithmetic without a calculator. An IGCSE maths home tutor in Mumbai will usually find that a capable student has outsourced fractions, surds, percentage reversals and index laws to a device sometime around Grade 8, and that the device is not available in the non-calculator paper. The Extended pair of papers, numbered Paper 2 and Paper 4 in the current Cambridge scheme, split along exactly this line, and your examinations officer can confirm the numbering and format for the session your child sits.

The second is method. Multi-step questions award marks for the route as well as the answer, so a student who writes nothing but a final figure throws away marks they had earned in their head. The fix is mechanical and slightly tedious: every line written down, every substitution shown, units carried through, the answer underlined. Tutors who mark in front of the student rather than taking the book away teach this fastest, because the student sees the mark being withheld and argues about it, which is the moment the habit changes.

The topics that catch students out are predictable. Bearings and trigonometry in three dimensions, vector geometry, transformations described in full, cumulative frequency and box plots read correctly, functions and their inverses, and algebraic fractions where a sign error early kills the whole question. A worked example that tells you more than any list: give a Grade 10 student a bearings question with a diagram they have to draw themselves, and the ones who can do trigonometry will still lose the question because the diagram was wrong. That is a reading and drawing failure, not a maths failure, and it is fixed in a fortnight.

sections.heading: How does the Mumbai school calendar squeeze Grade 10 maths?
paragraphs: The squeeze is November to February, and it comes from three things landing together: school mocks, board entry decisions and the May or June examination series. Families at Thakur International School in Kandivali East, Bombay Cambridge International School in Andheri East, Billabong High International School across Santacruz, Juhu, Malad and Thane, Witty International School in Malad and Chembur, JBCN International School at Parel and Borivali, NES International School in Mulund West, Smt Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul all work to that shape, though each school sets its own internal dates. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page.

Mock results in November and December are where tier conversations get real. A student placed in Core in Grade 9 on the strength of one bad Grade 8 test sometimes produces a mock that clearly belongs in Extended, and the window for changing an entry is set by the board and the school rather than by the family. Ask the examinations officer two questions in writing: what is the deadline for an entry change, and what evidence does the school want before making one. A tutor can help build that evidence in six weeks of marked past-paper work if the question is asked in November rather than in February.

Term planning follows from that. June to September is when a tutor can rebuild non-calculator arithmetic and algebra from the ground, which is slow work nobody wants to do in January. October and November are past-paper technique and mock preparation. December and January are error analysis on the mock scripts themselves, question by question. February and March are timed full papers under exam conditions. April is revision of the student's own mistake log and nothing new. Families who start in Grade 9 instead of Grade 10 get the whole sequence rather than the last third of it.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid for Grade 9 to 11 maths
paragraphs: Home tuition is the first choice for maths and the reason is physical: the tutor needs to see the working as it is produced, upside down, across a table, and reach over to point at the line where the sign changed. A tutor at home also sees the rest of the picture, including a student working on a bed with a phone face-up beside them. Families book an IGCSE maths home tutor in Mumbai for the same reason schools use whiteboards rather than screen shares for problem classes: pencil on paper, watched live, is still the fastest feedback loop anyone has found.

Online maths tuition has become genuinely good, with one requirement: a writing surface the tutor can see. A graphics tablet, a document camera or a phone on a stand pointed at the page all work. What fails is a student typing answers or holding a page up at the end. An IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai can be the better option when the subject route is unusual, since a 0607 specialist with a graphics calculator background may be two suburbs away or in another city altogether, and route knowledge beats proximity for that syllabus.

Hybrid suits Grade 10 and 11 best in the months when past papers dominate. One home tuition slot a week for new teaching and live marking, plus one short online session to go through a timed paper the student attempted alone, covers more ground than two home visits in the same week and costs less in travel. A home tutor for Mathematics (0580) Mumbai parents book in Grade 9 often shifts to exactly this pattern by Grade 11. During the monsoon, when Ghodbunder Road and the Andheri subway stop traffic for an evening, hybrid is also what keeps the week from being written off.
bullets: Home tuition lets the tutor watch working as it is written
Online needs a tablet, document camera or phone on a stand
Route specialists for 0607 may be worth reaching online
Hybrid fits past-paper season: teach live, review papers online
Monsoon evenings on Ghodbunder Road are why hybrid holds

sections.heading: What should I ask a maths tutor before the first session?
paragraphs: Ask three questions and listen to the structure of the answers. Which tier and which syllabus route have you taught most recently, and how many cohorts through. How do you handle a student who understands the lesson and loses marks in the exam. And what will you ask my child to do between sessions. A tutor who answers the second question with more practice is guessing; a tutor who answers it with a mistake log, timed single questions and a rule about writing every line has taught the problem before.

Our own checks sit behind that conversation. Identity and qualification documents are verified, teaching history is confirmed against the tiers and routes claimed, and references are called where a school or examination board is named. We do not grade tutors on charm, and we do not guarantee grades, because nobody honest in this business does. IB Gram is an independent platform with no affiliation to Cambridge, Pearson or any school listed here, which also means we have no interest in steering you towards one syllabus route over another.

There are two signals worth taking seriously yourself. A tutor who will mark a past-paper question in front of you is confident about method; a tutor who wants to take the book home and send comments later may be fine, but you learn less. And be wary of anybody offering a guaranteed grade, a fixed improvement or a jump of two bands by March, because examination boards do not work that way. Parents who search for the "best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai" get advertisements; parents who ask about tiers taught and marking habits get a tutor who fits. An IGCSE private tutor Mumbai families have kept for two years is the signal that matters.
bullets: Ask which tier and route the tutor has taught most recently
Ask what the student does between sessions, specifically
Watch the tutor mark a past-paper question in front of you
Be wary of a tutor promising a fixed grade improvement

sections.heading: What the tier decision does to a tuition plan
paragraphs: The tier decides what tuition is for. On Core, the honest aim is security: the full topic list covered properly, arithmetic without a calculator reliable, and every available mark on standard questions taken. Stretching a Core student with Extended material is a waste of the term unless the school has agreed to reconsider the entry. On Extended, the aim is the top end of the paper, which means multi-step problems, unfamiliar contexts and the discipline to leave a question and come back. Those are two different jobs, and a tutor who runs the same plan for both has not asked which tier you are on.

The decision also reaches forward. Students heading for Diploma Programme Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level need algebraic fluency that Core does not build, and schools look at the IGCSE tier when advising on DP routes. Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is a different destination with different demands. A Grade 9 family in Kandivali East asking whether the tier matters is really asking about Grade 11 subject choice two years out, and the answer is that it matters more there than it does on the certificate itself. The school's DP coordinator is the person to ask about route prerequisites.

Tier also moves the money, without anyone quoting a price. What IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on is the usual set: the board and route, the tier and level, how scarce that specialism is, how far the tutor travels and how long each session runs. Extended work with a Grade 11 student and marking between sessions prices differently from Core consolidation with a Grade 9 student in the same building. Ask any tutor for the per-session rate and what marking is included in it, and ask whether the rate changes in the exam term, because many quietly do.
bullets: Core tuition aims at full coverage and reliable standard-question marks
Extended tuition aims at multi-step problems and unfamiliar contexts
Tier influences advice on Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level
Scarcity, travel, session length and tier all move the rate

sections.heading: What four weeks of maths tuition can and cannot fix
paragraphs: Four weeks fixes habits, not topics. In a month you should see working written out properly, a mistake log that exists, and a student who attempts the second half of a long question instead of stopping. You should not expect the school mark to move yet, because the next assessment may be on a topic the tuition has not reached, and a single test is noise. The evidence at four weeks is in the exercise book: fewer blank spaces, more crossed-out first attempts, which looks worse and is better.

A term is long enough to judge properly. By then a student should be scoring consistently on past-paper questions in the topics covered, and the non-calculator work should no longer be the reason marks are lost. If the tutor has covered six topics and the student cannot reproduce question one from any of them unaided, the sessions are being spent on explanation rather than practice, and that is a conversation to have directly. Ask for the last three marked papers. Marked work that has stopped coming back is the clearest early sign a match is drifting.

Over one exam cycle the realistic target is a student who walks into the paper with timing rehearsed, a method habit that collects the marks they have earned, and a known list of their own recurring errors. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and publishes no success figures. If a match is not working, and the usual signs are sessions becoming chat, homework stopping and the student going quiet, tell us inside the first fortnight. We shortlist a replacement, pass on the topic coverage and the mistake log, and the new tutor starts from the student's real position rather than from the beginning.
bullets: Four weeks: written method, a mistake log, fewer abandoned questions
One term: consistent past-paper marks on topics actually covered
Ask for the last three marked papers at any review

sections.heading: Booking a maths home tutor in Mumbai this term
paragraphs: Bring four things to the first session and it pays for itself. The last two marked assessments, the topic list the teacher flagged, the mock paper or textbook so the tutor can see the route and tier, and the calculator the school expects the student to use in the examination. That last item surprises people. A student arriving at a session with a scientific calculator when the school runs a graphics-calculator syllabus has been practising on the wrong machine, and the tutor will spot it in the first ten minutes.

The session itself should end with three things said out loud: what the tutor thinks is causing the lost marks, what the first month covers, and what the student does between sessions. Write those down. A plan that is only in the tutor's head cannot be reviewed in November. An IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai worth keeping will also tell you what they are not going to do, such as teaching Additional Mathematics content to a student who needs the main syllabus secured first.

Then protect the slot. The families who get a full term of value are the ones who treat the weekly session like a school period rather than an appointment, and who tell the tutor about the school trip in October before it happens rather than on the day. If your child's week genuinely has no stable evening, say so at the start: a Saturday morning slot that holds beats a Tuesday that is cancelled twice a month, and the shortlist for weekend mornings is wider anyway, which works in your favour.
bullets: Bring two marked assessments and the flagged topic list
Bring the calculator the school expects in the examination
Get the first-month plan and homework expectation in writing
Treat the weekly slot like a school period, not an appointment
Weekend morning shortlists are wider than weekday evening ones

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE maths tutor in Mumbai cost per session?
faqs.answer: Rates are quoted per session and vary with five things, so ask about those rather than for a figure. The board and syllabus route matter, since a 0607 specialist with graphics-calculator experience is scarcer than a general maths tutor. The tier and year group matter, as Grade 11 Extended work carries marking between sessions. Travel distance matters, because a tutor crossing two suburbs is pricing an hour of road into every visit. Session length and frequency matter. IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai is usually agreed monthly, and the useful question is what marking and past-paper feedback the rate includes.

faqs.question: My son is in Core. Can he move to Extended?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the deadline belongs to the board and the school rather than to you. Schools usually place students on a tier in Grade 9 using Grade 8 performance, and a strong set of mocks can reopen the decision if it is raised early. Ask the examinations officer for the entry-change deadline and the evidence the school wants, in writing, in November. Six weeks of marked Extended past-paper work is the kind of evidence that gets looked at seriously. Leaving the request to February usually means the entry has closed, whatever the student can now demonstrate.

faqs.question: Can a tutor reach Kharghar for a 7pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided the tutor is based inside Navi Mumbai. Kharghar sits a short drive from Belapur, Nerul and Panvel along the Sion–Panvel Highway and Palm Beach Road, so a tutor from those nodes can hold a 7pm weekday slot for a full term without resenting it. Pulling someone across the creek from Chembur or Sion for the same slot works for a month and then quietly stops working. The Atal Setu has changed weekend logistics more than weekday ones, because the time saving is on the bridge rather than in the evening approach roads.

faqs.question: Does my child need a graphics calculator?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the syllabus route the school runs, which is why the paper header matters. Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics (0607) assumes a graphics calculator throughout. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics (0580) splits into a non-calculator paper and a calculator paper, with a scientific calculator for the second. Edexcel's International GCSE in Mathematics has its own requirements. Ask the maths department which model they teach from and buy that one, because a student who learns menus on a different machine loses time in the examination hall for no academic reason at all.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does Grade 10 maths need?
faqs.answer: One well-used session a week carries most students through Grade 10, with a second added in the term before the papers if past-paper timing is the weakness. Two sessions a week from September is usually a sign that something else is wrong, such as a topic backlog from Grade 9 that nobody has named. The variable that matters more than frequency is what happens between sessions. A student doing two timed questions and reviewing a mistake log every other day gains more from one weekly session than a student doing nothing between two.

faqs.question: Is online maths tuition as good as a tutor at home?
faqs.answer: For most students, home tuition is better for teaching and online is equal for review, which is why hybrid plans are common by Grade 11. In person, the tutor watches the working appear and interrupts at the line where it went wrong. Online can do the same with a graphics tablet or a document camera, and loses almost nothing for marking a paper the student has already attempted. Where online clearly wins is access to a route specialist who is not in your zone, and for families in Panvel, Kasarvadavali or Dahisar East that trade is often worth making.

faqs.question: He understands everything in class and still drops marks. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually because understanding a worked example and producing a solution under time pressure are different skills, and school teaching rewards the first. The common causes are specific: no written method, so earned marks are not awarded; arithmetic done mentally and wrongly without a calculator; misreading multi-part questions and answering part (b) with part (a) data; and no timing practice, so the last long question is never reached. Each one is fixable in weeks with timed single questions and marking done in front of the student. Ask the tutor to diagnose which of the four it is before planning anything.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor and my daughter do not get along?
faqs.answer: Tell us in the first fortnight and we shortlist someone else. Nobody benefits from a polite arrangement that limps to March, and the early signs are easy to read: the student stops asking questions, homework stops being done, the marked work stops coming back. When a replacement happens we pass on the topics covered so far and the student's error log, so the new tutor starts from her actual position. There is no awkward conversation to have with the outgoing tutor on your side either, because we handle that part of it.

faqs.question: Do we need a separate tutor for Additional Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the first question is whether the student should be taking it at all. Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics (0606) sits on top of the main syllabus and suits students with genuine algebraic fluency who are heading towards quantitative subjects at Diploma Programme level. A student still losing marks on the main syllabus should secure that first. Where a student is comfortable in both, one strong tutor can sometimes cover the pair in a longer weekly session, but ask specifically whether they have taught 0606 as a course rather than as enrichment topics.

faqs.question: What should a maths session at home look like in a small flat?
faqs.answer: A table, two chairs facing the same page, decent light and a plug point is the whole requirement. The dining table beats a bedroom desk because the tutor can sit beside rather than opposite the student and read the working the right way up. Keep the television off in the next room if the walls are thin, because maths sessions involve long silences while a student thinks and noise fills them. Phones go face-down on the table, not in a pocket. Families in compact two-bedroom flats in Mulund West and Chembur run home tuition like this routinely.

faqs.question: Will starting in Grade 11 be too late for the May series?
faqs.answer: Not too late, but it changes what tuition can realistically do. Starting in June of the examination year leaves time for topic repair, past-paper technique and timing, which is most of what moves marks. Starting in January means triage: the tutor picks the topics with the best return, drills method marks and timing, and leaves the rest. We will say so plainly rather than take the booking quietly. What nobody can do in a January start is rebuild two years of missing algebra, and any tutor promising otherwise is not being straight with you.

sections.heading: How IB Gram turns a May series request into a Mumbai shortlist
paragraphs: Most enquiries about IGCSE May and June exam preparation in Mumbai arrive as one line: Year 11, needs help, exams are in May. That is not enough to match on, and the gap between that line and a usable brief is where the first conversation goes. We ask four things. Which board the school entered your child for, because Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel set different papers for subjects with the same name. Which tier, where the subject has tiers. Which subjects are actually in trouble, as opposed to the ones that feel uncomfortable. And the week your school releases Year 11 for study leave, because that date decides whether the last stretch is evening work or daytime work.

With those four answers a shortlist takes shape quickly. A brief that reads all IB and IGCSE subjects means a tutor in Mumbai covering five courses at once, which is almost never what a family actually needs in the final year. A request for an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai who has taught the May series before is a narrower ask than it sounds: a tutor who has only ever taught the Years 9 and 10 part of the course has never watched a candidate under timetable pressure, never marked a full paper against the published mark scheme, and has no feel for how much ground a student can cover in a fortnight. Teaching history at paper and component level is the first filter we apply.

The second filter is geography, and in this city it is a hard constraint rather than a preference. A tutor in Nerul and a family in Khar West can agree on everything and still lose the arrangement by the fourth week, because the crossing is ninety minutes each way at the wrong hour. We match within the corridor first and only widen the search when a subject is genuinely scarce, at which point the honest answer is often online rather than a heroic commute nobody sustains through April.
bullets: 1. Send the board, the subject list and your child's school name.
2. We filter for tutors who have taught the May series itself.
3. You receive two or three profiles with paper-level teaching history.
4. A first session produces a written gap list before any term is booked.
5. Tell us within two sessions if the fit is wrong and we re-match.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE pathway is your child actually sitting in May?
paragraphs: Establish which course your child is entered for before you buy a single hour of tuition. In Mumbai this is less obvious than parents expect. Some schools run Cambridge IGCSE, some run the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and a number of schools enter candidates for both across different subjects, so a Year 11 student can be sitting a Cambridge science paper and an Edexcel mathematics paper in the same series. Several subjects also have tiers or routes, where one entry caps the available grades and the other opens the full range. Your school's examinations officer holds the entry record and can tell you exactly what was submitted. Ask for it in writing.

The pathway question also decides what the May series means for the year after. A student heading into the International Baccalaureate (IB) Diploma Programme (DP) is choosing Higher Level (HL) and Standard Level (SL) subjects during the same months as the run-up, often before any IGCSE result exists, which is why the Higher Level shortlist is built on mock performance and teacher judgement rather than on a grade in hand. A student moving to A Levels or to an Indian board faces a different conversation, with different subject prerequisites set by the receiving school.

For families arriving from the Middle Years Programme (MYP), the shift is real and it lands in Year 9 rather than Year 11. The Middle Years Programme assesses against criteria and rewards process; the IGCSE series rewards a specific written performance inside a fixed time against a published mark scheme. Students who were comfortable under criteria sometimes read their first terminal paper as unfair. It is not unfair, it is a different game, and the earlier a home tuition plan names that difference the less damage it does in May.
bullets: Get the entry record from the examinations officer, not from memory.
Confirm the tier or route for every subject with a choice.
Check whether two boards appear across your child's subject list.
Treat Higher Level choices as mock-driven, since results arrive later.
Ask the receiving school which subjects it requires for the next stage.

sections.heading: What the May series asks of a Year 11 candidate, subject by subject
paragraphs: The sciences carry an assessed practical element in most routes, and it is the part families forget until the week it is scheduled. Depending on the entry, that is either laboratory work or a written paper about experimental method, and either way it rewards something tuition can actually build: reading an unfamiliar method, spotting the controlled variable, drawing a results table before the data arrives. The precise structure, the components in play and how they fit together change with the syllabus version, so confirm the current shape with the Cambridge or Pearson subject guide for your child's year and with the subject teacher, not with a tutor's memory of an older cohort.

Mathematics splits by tier, and the two routes ask for different things. One rewards fluency and clean arithmetic under pressure; the other asks for unfamiliar problems that need a plan before a pen moves. There is also a calculator and non-calculator distinction in some routes, which matters more than it sounds because students who have only ever practised with a calculator lose marks on arithmetic they genuinely know. English divides again between a first-language route and a second-language route, with a coursework option in some entries and a fully examined option in others. Languages, drama and music usually have a performance or speaking component that the school schedules well before the written papers, which quietly moves a student's deadline forward by weeks.

The humanities and the commerce subjects are where home classes earn their keep fastest, because the content is usually known and the marks are lost in technique. A Business Studies candidate who writes everything she knows about a case study will score below a candidate who answers the command word asked. Geography source questions, History extract questions and Economics data response questions all reward the same discipline: read the stimulus, answer the question, stop. Art and Design runs on a long coursework portfolio with an internal submission date set by the school, which is the single most common reason a Year 11 student in Mumbai has no time for revision in February.
bullets: Confirm every component with the current subject guide for your year.
Ask when the school has scheduled speaking and practical components.
Treat the coursework submission date as the real February deadline.
Practise maths without a calculator if the route has such a paper.
Command words earn marks; everything a student knows does not.

sections.heading: Where in Mumbai May series tutors are placed, zone by zone
paragraphs: Mumbai, Maharashtra is six matching regions rather than one city, and the May run-up changes the calculation in each because study leave converts evening slots into daytime ones. In South Mumbai the distances are short and the clocks are slow: Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Peddar Road, Walkeshwar, Tardeo and Fort are all within a few kilometres of each other, but the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals can eat forty minutes of an evening, so we match within the island using the Western Line between Churchgate and Mumbai Central, the Harbour Line towards Dockyard, Metro Line 3 from Cuffe Parade to BKC and the Coastal Road, instead of pulling a tutor down from the suburbs for a 7pm session in April.

The Western Suburbs run north to south, and so does the matching. Bandra West, Khar West, Santacruz West and Juhu form one band; Andheri West, Versova and Oshiwara another; Goregaon East, Malad West, Kandivali East, Borivali and Dahisar another. Along the Western Line, the Western Express Highway, Link Road and Metro Lines 2A and 7 a tutor moves easily; across them, at 6pm, nobody does. The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line between Kurla and Mulund with Powai and Chandivali hanging off JVLR, and Powai is the awkward one because it has no station of its own, so tutors arrive by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar East, with Metro Line 1 and the Santacruz–Chembur Link Road doing the rest.

The Eastern Suburbs stretch from Chembur and Govandi up through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund West, served by the Central and Harbour lines and the Eastern Express Highway, with the Eastern Freeway putting South Mumbai within reach of Chembur and Wadala far faster than the map suggests. Navi Mumbai is matched node to node across Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel on Palm Beach Road and the Sion–Panvel Highway; the Atal Setu has shortened the crossing, but a weekday evening booking that depends on it rarely survives a full term. In Thane, Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Ghodbunder Road up to Kasarvadavali set the schedule, and a Thane tutor covers Thane.
bullets: South Mumbai is matched inside the island, not from the suburbs.
Western Suburbs matching runs along the line, never across it.
Powai and Chandivali are reached by road through JVLR.

sections.heading: How does the Mumbai school calendar line up with the May June series?
paragraphs: The Mumbai international school year opens in June and closes in April, which means a May series candidate gets one full academic year and no more. Schools split it around the Diwali break, so there is a long monsoon term and a shorter, much denser second term. At Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, at B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, at Ecole Mondiale World School in Juhu and at Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo the shape is broadly the same even where the dates differ: unit tests through the monsoon, coursework and mock windows across December and January, teaching wound up through February, and Year 11 released for study leave somewhere in the spring.

That calendar produces predictable pressure points, and they are not the ones parents brace for. The hardest fortnight of the year is usually not in May. It is the stretch in January when a mock timetable, an Art portfolio submission and a science practical assessment collide, because every one of those dates is set internally by the school rather than by the board. The second hardest is the first fortnight after study leave begins, when a student who has always worked to a school bell suddenly has eleven unstructured hours a day and no idea how to spend them. A home tuition schedule that shifts to mornings on the day study leave starts solves more of that than any amount of advice.

IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school named on this page; we name schools because their calendars shape the timing of the work, and for no other reason. The dates themselves are not ours to publish. The examination timetable, the entry deadlines, the late-entry window and the school's own internal submission dates come from your school's examinations officer, and they are the only authority worth planning against. Ask for the timetable the week it is released and put it on a wall where your child can see it.
bullets: The academic year runs June to April, so there is one year only.
January collides mocks, coursework and practicals in most schools.
Internal submission dates are set by the school, not by the board.
Shift sessions to mornings the week study leave begins.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or both in the run-up to May?
paragraphs: Home tutoring is the default for this request, and the reason is mechanical rather than sentimental. The May papers are written by hand, under time, on paper, and a student who has practised every question on a screen has not practised the thing being assessed. A home tutor sitting across the table watches the handwriting slow down at minute forty, sees the question that got skipped and came back to, and can time a full paper properly. For IGCSE May and June exam preparation in Mumbai that physical rehearsal is most of the value, and it is why an IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai arrangement usually beats the alternatives through the final term.

Online earns its place in two specific slots. The first is marking turnaround: a paper written on Saturday, photographed, marked overnight and discussed on a half-hour call on Sunday is faster than waiting for the next home visit, and the discussion is sharper because the script is fresh. The second is scarcity. An IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai may be the only realistic route to a specialist in a less commonly taught language or a minority option subject, and a tutor who knows that syllabus from two hundred kilometres away is worth more than a generalist who can reach your lobby in fifteen minutes. Screen fatigue is real, so keep online sessions shorter than home ones.

Hybrid is what most families settle into without planning it. Two home sessions a week for teaching and timed practice, one short online review for marked work, and a switch to full online for any week when the monsoon, an illness or a traffic collapse makes the journey unreliable. The honest trade-off is attention: a tired student at 8.30pm after a home session has little left for a screen, and a student who is alone in a room with a laptop will sometimes be alone in a room with a laptop and something else. Decide the mix deliberately with the tutor in the first week rather than drifting into it in March.
bullets: Handwritten timed practice is the strongest argument for home sessions.
Use online for overnight marking and next-day script discussion.
Scarce subjects are better taught online than taught badly nearby.
Keep online sessions shorter; attention falls faster on a screen.
Agree the home and online mix in week one, not in March.

sections.heading: What checks sit behind an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Every tutor listed on IB Gram has been through identity and qualification checks, and a teaching history that is specific enough to argue with. We record which board, which subjects, which components and which series a tutor has actually taught, because those four facts predict usefulness in the last term better than a degree certificate does. We take references, and for anyone who will sit in a family's living room we ask for the kind of detail a building's security desk will also ask for. A profile that cannot say which series a tutor last prepared a candidate for is a profile we do not publish.

There are checks only you can run, and they take one session. Hand the tutor a past paper question in your child's subject and ask them to mark it aloud against the published mark scheme. A specialist will tell you where the marks sit and where this answer threw one away; a generalist will say it looks good. Ask which series they prepared candidates for most recently and what went wrong in it. Ask what they would drop if there were only six weeks left. The answers to those three questions separate a subject teacher from a pleasant graduate with free evenings.

Be wary of a tutor who offers a guaranteed grade, and of anyone who quotes a number before seeing a script. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no honest tutor will either; what a good one will do is tell you which marks are reachable from here and which are not. Parents ask who the best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai is for the May papers, and the question has no answer in the abstract: the right tutor for a candidate two topics short in Chemistry is the wrong one for a candidate losing marks on essay structure. A search for IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai throws up plenty of confident promises, and the confident ones are usually the least informed. Check the paperwork, watch one session, and ask your child afterwards whether they understood the correction or only accepted it.
bullets: Board, subject, component and series are recorded on every profile.
Ask the tutor to mark a past paper question aloud.
Ask which series they last prepared a candidate for.
Ask what they would cut with six weeks remaining.
A tutor who promises a specific grade has not seen the script.

sections.heading: Working backwards from the May timetable, month by month
paragraphs: Sequencing is most of what IGCSE May and June exam preparation in Mumbai actually buys, so start at the papers and walk back. If the written series opens in the first half of May, revision has to be running by the start of April, which means syllabus coverage has to be finished in February, which means the mock results from December and January have to be acted on inside a fortnight rather than discussed at a parent meeting in March. Everything else follows from those three hinges. June and July, at the top of the Mumbai school year, are for a baseline: one past paper per subject sat properly, under time, so there is something real to measure against. August and September belong to content, and to the coursework pieces that are easiest to start and hardest to restart. October is the Diwali window and the first genuine catch-up block of the year; a student who is two topics behind in November is in a different situation from one who is two topics behind in February.

November and December carry drafts, internal deadlines and the first mock papers. Mocks are a diagnostic and a calendar marker here, nothing more: their job in this plan is to tell you which subjects need the second term and which can be left to the student. January is the collision month in most Mumbai schools, and the right response is triage rather than effort. Pick the two subjects where marked practice will move the most, and accept that the others get maintenance. February is when coverage closes. A tutor still teaching new content in March is a tutor who has run out of plan, and a student who has not finished the syllabus by the end of February will do better with ruthless prioritising than with a sprint through the last three chapters.

March is for full past papers under timetable conditions, marked by someone who knows the scheme, with the same mistakes hunted down twice. April is study leave, the longest uninterrupted study block your child will ever get and the easiest to waste; sessions move to mornings, the afternoon is for independent work, and the evening is for sleep rather than for another hour. Through May itself the work changes shape again, into the specific paper sitting in two days' time. If you are starting late, say in February with four subjects adrift, the realistic offer from a tutor is two subjects raised by technique and timing, not four subjects covered. Pick the two, say so out loud, and let the student stop carrying the other two as guilt.
bullets: Revision starts in April, so coverage must close in February.
June and July are for one properly timed paper per subject.
October's Diwali break is the last cheap catch-up window.
March is full papers under timetable conditions, marked properly.
Starting in February means choosing two subjects, not four.

sections.heading: What progress should look like at four weeks, one term and one series
paragraphs: At four weeks you are not looking for a better grade, you are looking for a change in method. A Year 11 student who has had four useful sessions can tell you what the command word in a question is asking for, will have started annotating a paper before answering it, and will be able to say where the marks sit in a six-mark question instead of writing until the space runs out. If none of that has changed after a month of home classes, the problem is the match or the diagnosis, and the right move is a conversation now rather than hope in March.

At one term the measurable thing is past-paper performance under time, compared against the baseline paper from the start. Expect the careless losses to fall first: the unit left off an answer, the graph axis unlabelled, the second part of a two-part question never attempted. Content gaps close more slowly and unevenly, and in a subject where a student missed a whole term to illness or to a school change, a single term of two sessions a week will not make that up. A tutor who says so in October is more useful than one who agrees with everything and tells you in March.

Across a full series the honest statement is narrow. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, cannot predict a paper, and will not publish a success rate, because a rate built on other families tells you nothing about your child's script. What a good arrangement does deliver is a student who knows the format, has sat every paper type under time, has had their own errors shown back to them, and walks into the hall without being surprised by anything except the content. The rest belongs to the examiner. Keep the plan, keep the sleep, and judge the tutor on the work you can see rather than on the result you cannot.
bullets: Four weeks: method changes, command words, annotation before answering.
One term: timed paper scores compared against the baseline paper.
Careless marks return first; content gaps close slowly.
A term of sessions cannot replace a missed school term.
Judge the tutor on visible work, not on a predicted outcome.

sections.heading: Getting started with May series home tuition in Mumbai
paragraphs: Bring four things to the first conversation and the match gets made in a day rather than a week. The subject list with the board and tier against each subject, taken from the entry record rather than from memory. The most recent report card and, if they exist, the actual mock scripts with the examiner's or teacher's marks on them, because a marked script tells a tutor more in five minutes than a transcript does in an hour. The school's study-leave date. And your honest ranking of which two subjects worry you most, which is almost never the same as the ranking of the lowest marks.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel like one. A good tutor will spend most of it watching your child work rather than talking: a timed question or two, a walk through a marked answer, a few questions about how revision currently happens. It ends with a written list of what needs covering, what needs practising and what gets dropped, with a sequence attached to the calendar months that are actually left. If the first session ends with nothing on paper, ask for it before booking a term.

After that the rhythm is simple and worth protecting. A standing weekly slot the family treats as fixed, one piece of written work done between sessions and marked before the next one, and a short review every few weeks against the month-by-month plan rather than against a feeling. Tell us early if a slot stops working, because a time that is wrong in November becomes a cancelled session in February. One arrangement covering all IB and IGCSE subjects through home classes Mumbai tutors can deliver sounds efficient and usually is not. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families need rarely exists in one person, and a two-tutor arrangement built deliberately works better than one tutor stretched across five subjects.
bullets: Have the entry record, with board and tier for each subject.
Bring marked mock scripts, not only the report card.
Expect a written gap list at the end of session one.
Protect one standing weekly slot the whole family plans around.
Two specialists usually beat one tutor stretched across five subjects.

faqs.question: How late is too late to start IGCSE May June exam preparation in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: February is late but workable; April is a rescue operation with narrow aims. Starting in February, a tutor can realistically lift two subjects through technique, timing and marked practice while the rest get maintenance. Starting once study leave has begun, the work becomes paper-specific: format, command words, mark allocation and the two or three topics most likely to appear in a question your child can actually answer. What no start date buys is full syllabus coverage in a month. The useful question to ask a prospective tutor is not whether they can finish the course, but which marks they think are reachable from where your child is now. Families who begin IGCSE May and June exam preparation in Mumbai around the Diwali break rarely have to ask it at all.

faqs.question: Can a tutor travel to our building in Bandra West for an evening slot in the final term?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the slot time matters more than the distance. A tutor matched within the Bandra, Khar and Santacruz band reaches a Bandra West building reliably at 6.30pm or 7.30pm; the same tutor coming from Mulund or Kharghar will manage it in November and start arriving late by February. Give us the building name and the gate protocol when you enquire, because societies that require a pre-registered visitor entry for a standing weekly slot are far easier to set up once than renegotiated every week. Also tell us whether the lift and the study space are shared, since that decides the realistic session length.

faqs.question: Should a parent be at home during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: Someone should be in the flat, but not in the room. An adult at home is a sensible condition for any tutor working with a minor, and most families here treat it as standard. Sitting in on the session is different and usually counterproductive: a Year 11 student who is being watched by a parent will stop admitting what they do not understand, which is the single most useful thing that happens in a diagnostic hour. Leave the door open, stay within earshot, and ask your questions afterwards. If you want to see the method, ask the tutor for ten minutes at the end of the session instead.

faqs.question: How many subjects can we realistically take on before the May series?
faqs.answer: Two with real depth, three at a stretch, and five only if you are paying for supervision rather than teaching. Each subject needs a timed paper, marking turnaround and a session to discuss the script, and that cycle takes time the student also needs for school work and sleep. Families who spread tuition across every subject in January usually end up with five arrangements that each move nothing. Rank the subjects by how far marked practice can move them rather than by how low the last report was, then commit to the top two. The remaining subjects are often better served by the school's own revision sessions.

faqs.question: Do you cover both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel subjects at IGCSE level?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we filter by board before anything else, because the papers differ even where the subject names match. A tutor who has prepared candidates for a Cambridge International Education syllabus is not automatically useful for the Pearson Edexcel version of the same subject, and the mark schemes reward slightly different things. Tell us which board appears against each subject on the entry record and we match accordingly. Where a student is sitting both boards across different subjects, which happens in several Mumbai schools, we will usually suggest two tutors rather than one generalist covering both.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Fees move with five things, and none of them is a fixed city rate. The board and level, since a terminal-year specialist costs more than a Year 9 generalist. Subject scarcity, which is why a common science is easier to staff than a minority language. Travel distance and the time of day, because a tutor crossing a zone at 6pm is selling two hours of travel alongside the lesson. Session length and frequency. And whether the work includes marking written papers between sessions, which is real hours. We will not publish a price list here; ask for the specific quote against your own subject list and slot. Put the same question to any IGCSE private tutor Mumbai parents recommend to you, because those five factors apply to them too.

faqs.question: What happens to the schedule once school releases Year 11 for study leave?
faqs.answer: The schedule should change shape on the first day, not drift. Study leave converts evening slots into morning ones, and morning is when a timed paper is worth sitting, so we move sessions to the daytime wherever the tutor's other commitments allow. The afternoon belongs to independent work on whatever the morning exposed, and the evening is for stopping. Families who keep the old 7.30pm slot through study leave tend to get a tired student doing their worst work at the hardest hour. Flag the study-leave date when you first enquire so the tutor's daytime availability is checked before you book.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for a family in Thane in the last six weeks before the May papers?
faqs.answer: It works for marking and review, less well for timed rehearsal. A Thane family on Ghodbunder Road or near Pokhran Road often has a genuine choice between a local tutor who arrives in twenty minutes and a specialist elsewhere in Mumbai who is only reachable on a screen. For the last six weeks, the compromise most families land on is handwritten papers sat at home under time, photographed and sent, then discussed on a short call the next day. That keeps the physical rehearsal where it belongs and uses the screen for the part it is actually good at, which is fast feedback on a fresh script.

faqs.question: What if the tutor is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: Tell us in week two rather than week six, and we re-match without an argument. A mismatch in the final year is expensive in a way it is not in Year 9, because the weeks do not come back. The signals worth acting on are specific: no written work is coming back marked, your child cannot say what the last session was about, or the sessions have quietly become homework supervision. We will ask what the first tutor did and did not do, use that to narrow the replacement, and pass the diagnostic notes across so the new tutor does not spend a session rediscovering the same gaps.

faqs.question: Where do the December and January mocks fit into a May series plan?
faqs.answer: They are the hinge the second term turns on, and their job here is to allocate effort. A mock paper tells you which subjects will respond to marked practice and which are short of content, and it does that in a way no report card can. Act on the results within a fortnight: pick the subjects, change the plan, book the slots. The grade on a mock is a snapshot taken before revision began, so treat it as information rather than as a forecast. How to prepare for the mocks themselves is a separate question with a separate answer; here, what matters is the fortnight after them.

faqs.question: Who confirms the exam timetable and the entry deadlines?
faqs.answer: Your school's examinations officer, and only them. Schools submit entries on the board's schedule, hold the candidate statement of entry, and publish the local sitting times for each paper, including any clash arrangements where two of your child's papers fall together. IB Gram does not hold that information for your school and will not quote dates at you; a tutor who recites a timetable from memory is reciting last year's. Ask the examinations officer for the statement of entry as soon as it is issued, check every subject and tier on it against what you believe your child is studying, and raise any discrepancy immediately.

igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.closingCta: Send us the subject list with the board against each subject, your child's school, your area and the two evenings that are genuinely free. We come back with two or three IGCSE specialists who have taught the May series, their component-level teaching history, and slots that fit your corridor. You pick one, the first session produces a written gap list mapped to the months left, and you decide about a term after that.
