sections.heading: What should you check before adding a third tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Check the obvious things about the person, then check two things about the household. On the person: the subject degree, the teaching qualification, whether they have taught your board to a real final series rather than only up to Year 10, and whether they will mark written work between sessions. IB Gram verifies identity, degree, teaching qualification and the school or institution where a tutor teaches or has taught, and does not represent anyone as approved or endorsed by a board or a school. That part is standard and should take one conversation.

The household checks are the ones people skip. First, count the hours. Add up school, existing tutoring, existing homework and the new tutor's homework, and look at what is left in a weekday evening. If the answer is that something has to give, the new tutor will not work however good they are, and the honest conclusion is to swap rather than add. Second, write down what the third tutor is for in one sentence with a measurable end. If you cannot write that sentence, you are not ready to engage anyone, and the conversation to have is with the school rather than with a tutor.

Ask the new tutor one question the other two were probably never asked: what would make you tell us to stop? A tutor who has an answer, something like once she is consistently securing the marks in the written paper without prompting, is somebody thinking about your child rather than about a standing slot. A tutor with no answer to that question will be with you for two years by default. Parents hunting for the best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai often judge on explanation and rapport, which matter, but this one question tells you more about the next two years than either.

Finally, check the overlap. Two tutors covering Physics and Chemistry will both teach the same quantitative skills, and two language tutors will both teach essay structure. That overlap is not waste if it is acknowledged and divided, and it is pure waste if neither knows the other exists. Tell each tutor who else is working with your child and on what. Most will adjust willingly, and some will tell you outright that a subject they would otherwise have taught is already covered, which is the sort of honesty worth keeping.
bullets: Verify degree, teaching qualification and final-series experience on your board
Count the total weekly hours before adding anybody to the set
Write one sentence saying what the new tutor is for, with a measurable end
Ask each tutor what would make them tell you to stop
Tell every tutor who else is working with your child, and on what

sections.heading: Setting a ceiling before your first IGCSE home tuition enquiry
paragraphs: A ceiling is a number of concurrently tutored subjects, decided by the household before anybody is contacted, written down somewhere both parents can see. Expressed that way it is enforceable, because counting subjects requires no spreadsheet and no argument about what is affordable this particular month. Two is a common and workable ceiling for a student in Years 9 and 10. Three is defensible in the exam year. Four is where most families lose both the thread and the student's week, and almost nobody arrives at four on purpose. The ceiling matters precisely because it is set while you are calm, and every subsequent decision is made while you are not.

The mechanism that defeats families without one is simple and almost invisible. Each addition is evaluated alone and against a sympathetic case: a worried subject teacher, a disappointing test, a friend's child who has a tutor for it. Evaluated alone, every single addition passes. The question nobody asks at that moment is whether this subject is more deserving than the three already being funded, and that is the only question that would have produced a different answer. A ceiling forces that comparison, because the only way to say yes is to say no to something else.

Review the whole set together, once a term, at a fixed date. Put all the tutors on one page with three columns: what this subject was for, what has changed, and whether it continues. Reviewing tutors one at a time always produces continuation, because each individual tutor is producing something and the conversation feels like an evaluation of a person. Reviewing them together produces a ranking, and a ranking produces a decision. That is the entire difference, and it is why the whole exercise should take twenty minutes once a term rather than being left to a vague sense that things are fine.

Then treat every escalation as a swap. When the mock results arrive in the new year and a new subject looks urgent, the ceiling is already set and the question becomes which existing arrangement ends. Families who have practised this twice find it unremarkable. Families meeting it for the first time in February find it agonising, add the fourth, and discover in March that the student has stopped completing anything for anybody. What keeps IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai under control is almost never a better price. It is a count of home tuition arrangements agreed in advance and held.
bullets: A ceiling is a count of concurrently tutored subjects, agreed before any enquiry
Two subjects is workable in Years 9 and 10; three is defensible in the exam year
Every addition evaluated alone will pass; the ceiling forces a comparison
Review all tutors on one page once a term, never one tutor at a time
Treat every new subject as a swap, decided before the mock results land

sections.heading: What would have to be true for this tuition to stop?
paragraphs: Ask that question on day one and write the answer down, because tuition that has no stopping condition becomes a standing household commitment that nobody re-examines for two years. The answer should be observable rather than aspirational. He completes a full past paper under timed conditions without prompting. She stops losing method marks in multi-step working. He brings the right questions to the session instead of waiting to be given them. Those are conditions a parent can check. A target grade is not, because it depends on a paper nobody has seen.

At four weeks across a multi-subject set, the thing to look at is the week rather than the marks. Is the student completing what each tutor sets? If three tutors are each reporting incomplete work, the problem is not three weak students in one child; it is that the set is too large and the ceiling has already been breached. That is a scheduling conclusion, not an academic one, and acting on it at four weeks is far cheaper than acting on it in March.

At one term, the review page tells you what to do. Expect uneven results across the set, with the subjects worked hardest moving and the others holding, and expect at least one arrangement to be producing less than the others. Ending that one is not a failure of the tutor; it is the review working as intended, and it is what creates room for the subject that will matter more next term. At one full exam cycle, from the first mocks to the final series, what families consistently report is that two well-supported subjects moved further than four lightly-supported ones.

The limits are worth stating plainly. IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no tutor listed here can promise an IGCSE outcome at any level of spending. Tuition raises the quality of the hours a student puts in; it does not control the paper, the day or the other six days of the week. Nobody should ever be told that a higher commitment buys a safer result, and a family being told so should treat it as a reason to walk away rather than a reason to pay more.
bullets: Define an observable stopping condition on day one and write it down
Four weeks: if several tutors report incomplete work, the set is too large
One term: expect uneven results and end the weakest arrangement deliberately
Two well-supported subjects usually beat four lightly-supported ones
IB Gram does not guarantee grades and no level of spending can

sections.heading: Starting IGCSE home tutor support in Mumbai with a ceiling in place
paragraphs: Before you contact anybody, agree three things at home. The ceiling, meaning how many subjects will be supported at once this term. The ranking, meaning which subjects those are and in what order they would be dropped. And the review date, which goes in the calendar now rather than being left to a moment of concern. Those three decisions take one conversation over a weekend and they shape the whole of the next two years.

Then send one enquiry covering everything rather than three separate ones over three months. Include the board your school runs, every subject you are considering, your child's year, the Core or Extended entry where it is settled, your locality and your realistic weekday window. A single enquiry lets the whole set be matched inside one pocket of the city, which is what makes it sustainable, and it lets somebody point out when two of your requested subjects could sensibly be covered by one specialist.

The first session with each tutor is diagnostic. Expect the tutor to spend most of it watching your child work rather than talking, and expect a one-sentence conclusion at the end naming which of four things is the real problem: reading the question, setting the work out, knowing the content, or managing the time. Collect those sentences across your tutors and read them together. More often than you would expect, two tutors name the same underlying problem, and fixing that one thing does more than either subject arrangement would have done alone.

After that, run it. Hold the standing slots, keep one folder per subject, and meet the review date whatever is happening that week. If an arrangement is not working, say so and an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai from a different match is arranged without penalty or notice period. And if the review says you are funding one subject too many, act on it that week rather than at the end of term, because a ceiling that bends once stops being a ceiling at all.
bullets: Agree the ceiling, the ranking and the review date before contacting anyone
Send one enquiry covering every subject rather than three over three months
Expect a diagnostic first session and a one-sentence conclusion from each tutor
Read the tutors' conclusions together; two often name the same root problem
Act on the review in the same week, or the ceiling stops meaning anything

faqs.question: How many subjects should a family realistically fund tutoring for at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Two at once is workable for most students in Years 9 and 10, and three is defensible in the exam year when mocks expose a specific gap. Four is where arrangements usually break, not because of cost but because the student is carrying four sets of tutor homework on top of the school's, and the week stops closing. The honest test is not what the household can sustain financially but what the student can complete. If work is going unfinished across several subjects, you are past the ceiling, and adding a fifth tutor to fix it makes the problem worse rather than better.

faqs.question: Every subject teacher says my child needs extra help. How do I choose between them?
faqs.answer: Rank the subjects on three questions rather than on who sounded most concerned. Which is closest to a genuine problem, as opposed to a subject your child dislikes? Which has the largest downstream consequence, meaning it gates a Diploma Programme choice or a university prerequisite? And which is already being supported well by the school, so outside help would duplicate it? Answering those in order usually reduces four requested subjects to two that matter now. Tell the other teachers you are prioritising and will reconsider next term. Most respond well, and some will tell you frankly that their subject can wait.

faqs.question: Should we review each tutor separately or all of them together?
faqs.answer: All of them together, on one page, once a term. Reviewing tutors individually almost always produces continuation, because each tutor is visibly producing something and the conversation feels like a judgement on a person. Reviewing them side by side produces a ranking instead, and a ranking produces a decision. Use three columns: what this subject was for, what has changed since, and whether it continues. The exercise takes twenty minutes and it is the only point in the year when anybody looks at the total rather than at one arrangement in isolation. Put the date in the calendar at the start.

faqs.question: Why is it so hard to find an extra tutor in January and February?
faqs.answer: Because the whole city tries at once. First mock results land within weeks of each other across Mumbai international schools, every family reaches the same conclusion simultaneously, and tutors who held two free evenings in September hold none. Subject specialists go first, and the scarcer the subject the earlier they go. The constraint at that point is tutor hours, not your budget. The fix is to reserve exam-term capacity with your existing tutors in the quiet months, and to identify and meet a likely exam-term tutor in October rather than discovering in January that nobody is available.

faqs.question: We have a Year 11 child in Kharghar and a Year 9 sibling. Can we support both at once?
faqs.answer: You can, but stagger them rather than stacking them, because the peak months collide. The younger child's transition into the IGCSE years and the elder's mock season both want support in the same term, and a household in Kharghar or Nerul also faces a thinner local pool once it needs two different subject specialists in Navi Mumbai at the same time. Start the younger sibling in the quiet part of the year, reduce or pause during the elder's exam term, and resume afterwards. Discuss the planned pause with the tutor at the outset so it is expected rather than abrupt.

faqs.question: Our tutor comes to Thane on a weekday evening. Does distance really affect what we pay?
faqs.answer: Yes, though in Thane it shows up in availability as much as in cost. The run from Thane station out along Pokhran Road and Majiwada to Ghodbunder Road and Kasarvadavali can take twenty minutes off-peak and most of an hour at seven, and a tutor absorbing that twice has a shorter evening to offer anybody. A family funding three subjects here should staff all three from the same side of Ghodbunder Road. Scattering tutors across the stretch produces a set that works in July and falls apart in the monsoon, and every replacement restarts the arrangement from scratch.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to use one tutor for several subjects instead of a specialist each?
faqs.answer: It usually looks simpler and rarely works across more than two subjects. A tutor strong in Physics and Mathematics can genuinely carry both, because the skills overlap. The same person added onto English Literature or a second language is typically learning the paper alongside your child, and you end up paying for coverage rather than teaching. The sensible compromise is to pair subjects that genuinely share skills under one specialist and match the rest separately. Ask any tutor offering several subjects which of them they have taught to a real final series, and treat the others as untested.

faqs.question: Does somebody need to be home when three different tutors come through the week?
faqs.answer: Somebody should be in the flat, though not in the room, and the practical issue with several tutors is the gate rather than the supervision. Register all your tutors with the society office at the start of the term as standing weekly visitors, with their days and times, instead of clearing each one individually every week. A tutor arguing at security for ten minutes loses ten minutes of the session, and with three tutors that happens three times a week. Keep one folder per subject in a fixed place so each tutor finds their own material without anybody hunting for it.

faqs.question: Our child says they want to drop a particular tutor. Should we listen?
faqs.answer: Listen, but do not decide on it. A fifteen-year-old will almost always nominate the strictest tutor, and the strictest tutor is usually the one setting and marking the most work. What is worth taking seriously is a specific complaint: the tutor explains the same way twice, never marks anything, or talks over them. That is actionable and worth raising. A general dislike is not a reason to drop a subject, especially a prerequisite one. Decide the drop on your review page using the subject's purpose and progress, then tell your child the reasoning so the decision does not look arbitrary.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai actually depend on?
faqs.answer: Board, tier, subject scarcity, travel distance and session length, in roughly that order of predictability. Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel differ in paper design; Extended preparation is more demanding than Core; a tutor crossing the city gives up their evening. Scarcity is the strongest factor, which is why Additional Mathematics, Economics and second-language support are harder to staff than general Mathematics. For a household funding several subjects, the practical consequence is that the subjects added last are usually the unusual ones and therefore the hardest to arrange, which is another reason to decide the full set early rather than one subject at a time.

faqs.question: What happens if one of our tutors is not working out mid-term?
faqs.answer: Tell us and a replacement is matched for that subject, with no penalty and no notice period beyond the courtesy of telling the tutor. Before replacing, though, check the review page: sometimes the right answer is not a different tutor for that subject but no tutor for that subject, because the set is too large and this was the arrangement that was always going to fail first. Replacing automatically is how a household ends up back at four tutors having told itself it only swapped one. Three sessions with a new match is normally enough to know.

faqs.question: Will spending more on tutoring make a better grade more likely?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and nobody should tell you otherwise. Beyond the point where a student has strong support in the subjects that genuinely need it, extra spending buys more homework rather than more learning, and the student's week is what fails. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, no tutor here can promise an IGCSE outcome, and a family being offered a guaranteed result in exchange for a larger commitment should treat that as a reason to walk away. What is worth funding is defined, reviewed and limited: a named problem, an observable stopping condition, and a ceiling the household agreed before the first enquiry.

igcse-tuition-fees.closingCta: Send one enquiry covering every subject you are weighing, with the board your school runs, your child's year, your Mumbai locality and your weekday window. Say how many subjects you intend to support at once, because that ceiling shapes the whole match. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families need is staffed inside one pocket of the city wherever possible, and the review date goes in the calendar before the first session happens.

sections.heading: How IB Gram sets a realistic radius for IGCSE tuition near me in Mumbai
paragraphs: The first thing we ask after the subject is the year group, because the year group sets the time budget and the time budget sets the radius. A Year 9 student has slack in the week. They can travel to a tutor, or accept a tutor who arrives a little late because of a long run across the city, and the cost is absorbed somewhere in a lighter homework load. A Year 11 student in the second half of the course has no slack at all, and every minute spent in transit is taken from revision, sleep or the one evening they are not doing anything. Treating those two students as the same matching problem is the most common planning mistake we see.

The process runs in this order. 1. Subject, board and year group, which together tell us how scarce the tutor pool is and how much time the student actually has. 2. A time budget rather than a distance: how many minutes a week your family can genuinely give to travel, counting both directions and counting the settling time at each end. 3. A radius derived from that budget, which for a Year 9 family is often generous and for a Year 11 family is usually the building, the lane or the node. 4. A match inside that radius wherever the subject supply allows, and an honest conversation about online when it does not. 5. A review date set for the end of the current term, so the radius is revisited deliberately rather than when it breaks.

Step five is the one families skip and the one that saves the arrangement. Nearly every long-distance tuition arrangement in this city ends the same way: it works for two terms, the student gets busier, the tutor gets busier, somebody starts arriving fifteen minutes late, and by February the sessions have quietly become fortnightly. Nobody decided that. It happened because the radius was set once, in a calm month, and never looked at again. Put a date in the calendar at the start of each term to ask whether the travel is still worth what it costs, and you will make that decision while you still have options. A search for IGCSE tuition near me in Mumbai is really a search for a radius you can still live with in February.

sections.heading: The IGCSE workload curve from Year 9 to Year 11
paragraphs: IGCSE is examined at the end of a two-year course, and the workload across those two years is not a straight line. Year 9 is foundation work, with internal testing that feels serious to the student and is mostly diagnostic to the school. Year 10 is where the content arrives in volume and where most schools fix setting and route decisions. Year 11 is examination preparation layered on top of coursework that is still being completed, which is why it feels disproportionately heavy to families who planned on the basis of the previous year. Two boards run here, Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel, and while the curve is similar under both, the coursework weighting differs by subject and is worth checking early.

The Core and Extended decision steepens that curve for some students. Where both routes exist, Core limits the achievable grade and Extended opens the range at the cost of more content and harder papers. A student moved up to Extended in Year 10 has effectively added a subject's worth of work to a year that was already the heaviest, and that is precisely the moment a long weekly commute to tuition stops being affordable. Families who intend to push for Extended should assume the radius will need to shrink a term earlier than they expected.

Beyond Year 11 the same logic repeats. The International Baccalaureate Diploma Programme (DP) requires three subjects at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), and the HL subjects carry Internal Assessment (IA) work that makes the DP years busier again. Mumbai schools generally gate HL entry on the IGCSE grade profile, so a Year 10 student aiming at Mathematics or Physics at HL needs the support now, when there is still room in the week to travel for it. The honest summary is that the amount of travel a family can sustain falls every year from Year 9 onwards and never rises again.
bullets: Year 9 diagnostic, Year 10 content-heavy, Year 11 coursework plus examinations
Coursework weighting differs by subject across Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel

sections.heading: Which subjects tolerate a long trip and which do not
paragraphs: Across all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 a tutor in Mumbai covers, travel tolerance varies by the kind of work the session involves. Mathematics is the most robust. A student who arrives tired can still do a worked problem set, and a sixty-minute Mathematics session with a slightly late start is still a useful session. The Sciences sit in the middle: content teaching survives a rushed arrival, but data-response and practical-paper work needs a settled student with a printed paper in front of them, and that work is exactly what Year 11 needs most.

English Language and Literature are the least travel-tolerant subjects on the timetable. Directed writing and timed reading responses require a student who is mentally present from the first minute, and a teenager who has just spent forty minutes in a car arrives nowhere near that state. The same is true of the second languages, where oral practice depends on confidence and confidence does not survive being flustered. If your child's weak subject is English Literature and the only available tutor is an hour away, the honest answer is usually to find someone closer or go online, even if the distant tutor is the stronger teacher on paper.

Session length interacts with all of this. Coursework sessions, including the project work in Computer Science and Global Perspectives and the drafting work in Business Studies and Economics, need ninety minutes to be worth anything, because the first twenty are spent finding where the student left off. Pure revision and past-paper marking work well in sixty. A family paying for travel on a sixty-minute session is paying a high overhead for a short lesson, which is an argument for either lengthening the session or shortening the trip. Most families arranging all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Mumbai find the sensible pattern is longer sessions less often as the year gets heavier, not shorter sessions more often.

sections.heading: How far is realistic from your part of Mumbai
paragraphs: Mumbai, Maharashtra is six practical tutoring markets rather than one, and knowing which one you are in tells you how wide your realistic radius is before you start. South Mumbai is compact and self-contained. Families in Colaba, Cuffe Parade, Churchgate, Fort, Babulnath, Walkeshwar, Peddar Road, Tardeo, Worli and Parel can usually arrange home tuition inside the island, and should, because bringing a tutor down from the suburbs for a weekday evening is an arrangement with a short natural life. For these families IGCSE tuition near me in Mumbai genuinely does mean near, and that is an advantage rather than a limitation. The Western Line out of Churchgate and Grant Road, the Harbour Line towards Dockyard, Metro Line 3 and the Coastal Road all serve the zone, which means the options are real even when the radius is small.

The Western Suburbs are the deepest market and the most linear. Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz West, Juhu, Vile Parle, Andheri West and East, Oshiwara, Goregaon East, Malad, Kandivali East, Borivali and Dahisar East sit along the Western Line, Metro Lines 2A and 7, Metro Line 1 from Versova to Ghatkopar, the Western Express Highway and Link Road, with the Bandra-Worli Sea Link connecting the southern end to Worli. Families here have the widest choice and consequently the greatest temptation to overreach, agreeing in June to a tutor four suburbs away because the match looked ideal. The Central Suburbs around Powai, Chandivali, Kanjurmarg, Ghatkopar and Kurla are linked by JVLR, the Eastern Express Highway and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road, and Powai in particular tends to recruit from Andheri East and Ghatkopar rather than from within.

The Eastern Suburbs run Chembur, Govandi, Wadala, Bhandup and Mulund, served by the Central and Harbour lines, the Eastern Express Highway, the Eastern Freeway and the Monorail from Chembur to Wadala. Navi Mumbai is nodal and each node is close to the next, so Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar, Airoli and Panvel families should match within the node or the neighbouring one, using Palm Beach Road and the Harbour Line, with the Atal Setu now making a South Mumbai arrangement thinkable in a way it was not before, though still not for a Tuesday evening in Year 11. Thane runs its own market from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada and Hiranandani Estate out along Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali, fed by the Central Line and the Trans-Harbour Line. In every zone the rule is the same: the wider you start, the sooner you will have to narrow, so start narrow in Year 10 if Year 11 matters to you.

sections.heading: Why does the Mumbai school day get longer exactly when you need it shorter?
paragraphs: Because Year 11 schools add time rather than remove it. From around October onwards, most Mumbai international schools layer extra revision classes, practical sessions, oral assessments and remedial periods on top of the ordinary timetable, and much of that lands after the normal end of the school day. A student who was free at three in Year 9 is often not free until five in Year 11, and the journey home has not got shorter. That is the squeeze, and it arrives at the same time as mocks and coursework deadlines rather than conveniently before them.

The calendar makes the shape clear. The academic year opens in June, internal testing starts late in the first term, and the October assessments before the Diwali break are the first honest signal. December and January carry mock examinations and the bulk of coursework submission, and in several subjects the oral and practical components are scheduled internally in that same window. February and March are the final run-up. A family carrying ninety minutes of weekly travel into that period is spending the equivalent of a full revision session every week on transport, and in January that is not a reasonable trade.

Schools are named on this page only because Mumbai families attend them and their calendars create these pressure points. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school or examination board mentioned anywhere on this site. What we would say plainly is that the squeeze is predictable. It happens to every cohort, in every school, in the same months, and it is therefore something to plan for in August rather than something to react to in January when the options have narrowed to whatever is physically closest.

sections.heading: Should IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai move online in the final year?
paragraphs: Only for the travel it actually saves, and only if the subject allows it. Home tuition is the lead service on every IB Gram page because it works: an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai at the table sees the working, takes the pen and catches the moment a student stops following. If your tutor lives ten minutes away, nothing about Year 11 should change that. The question only arises when the travel is long, and then the honest comparison is not home against online. It is a shorter home session plus a long trip against a full online session with no trip at all. Framed that way, home classes with a nearby tutor usually win and home classes with a distant one usually do not.

Where online genuinely wins is the final term, for a specific subject, with a tutor the student already knows. The relationship is established, the tutor already understands how this student thinks, and the only thing being removed is the commute. That is the best version of the switch. The worst version is moving online in January with a tutor your child has never met, which combines the hardest month with the hardest mode and a stranger. If you are going to use online in Year 11, start it in Year 10 with someone the student already trusts, so the mode is familiar before the pressure arrives.

The middle option is the one most families end up preferring. Keep the in-person session for the subject that needs a person in the room, usually English or anything involving drafting, and move the lighter revision subject online. That keeps the total travel inside a budget the week can bear without giving up the thing that makes home tuition worth paying for. A family running an IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai for Mathematics revision and an in-person tutor for English Literature has usually thought about this properly, whether or not they would describe it that way.
bullets: No reason to change mode if the tutor is already ten minutes away
Compare a short home session plus travel against a full online session

sections.heading: Checking a tutor, and checking a tutor change
paragraphs: Standard checks come first. Government photographic identification is confirmed, the degree or teaching qualification claimed is confirmed, and the tutor is asked which boards and which year groups they have actually taught rather than studied. Board experience carries real weight here: someone who has never worked through a Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel mark scheme will teach sound content and still cost a student presentation marks. References from previous teaching or tutoring work are taken where they exist. You should expect all of this and you should ask for it if it is not offered.

What you check yourself is fit, in the first twenty minutes of the first session. Does the tutor ask your child questions or talk at them. Do they ask to see the school's marked work. Do they say openly when they do not know something. An IGCSE private tutor in Mumbai who admits a gap in the first hour is usually still useful six months later, because they will prepare rather than improvise.

There is a second kind of check that this page cares about more, and it applies when you are changing tutor because of distance. A new tutor needs to be told what the previous one was doing, and almost nobody does this. Write down, in five lines, which topics were covered, where the student was weak, what the current coursework position is and what the previous tutor had planned next. Hand that to the new tutor before the first session. Without it, the new arrangement spends three weeks rediscovering what the old one already knew, and three weeks in the final year is most of the gain you were trying to capture by moving closer. The handover note is the cheapest part of a tutor change and the part that most often does not happen.
bullets: Photographic identification and qualifications confirmed before introduction
Board and year-group teaching experience asked for specifically
Judge fit yourself in the first twenty minutes of session one

sections.heading: When should you move IGCSE tuition closer, and when is it too late?
paragraphs: Move it at the end of Year 10 or during the first term of Year 11, and treat the end of the first term as the deadline. The reason is arithmetic rather than opinion. A tutor change costs roughly a month: a settling session, a diagnostic period, and the time it takes a new teacher to learn how your child thinks. Made in June or August, that month is spent in the cheapest part of the year and fully repaid by the travel saved over the following three terms. Made in January, the same month is spent in the single most valuable weeks of the course, and the travel saved between January and the examinations will never add up to what that month was worth. Changing tutor in the final term usually costs more than the travel it saves. That is the honest point of this page.

There is a second party to this decision and families forget about them. A tutor's willingness to travel is not fixed either. In June, with a half-empty diary, a good tutor will happily agree to cross three suburbs for a single Tuesday family. By November, with the week full of students who live closer, that same trip is the weakest hour in their schedule, and what happens next is rarely a conversation. It is a slow drift: a request to move the slot later, a reschedule, a cancelled week. If your arrangement depends on a tutor making an unusually long journey, assume it is fragile by the second term and plan accordingly rather than feeling betrayed when it frays.

So plan the shrink instead of scrambling. Three practical moves. First, when you set up tuition in Year 9 or Year 10, ask the tutor directly whether they could still do this journey if their diary were full, and listen to the pause. Second, identify in advance which subject you would move online first if the week tightened, and tell the tutor that is the plan, so the switch is a known contingency rather than a surprise. Third, if you are already in Year 11 with a long-distance tutor who is working well, the default answer is to keep them and change the mode, not the person. Searching for IGCSE tuition near me in Mumbai in January and replacing a tutor who understands your child in order to save forty minutes is the wrong trade in almost every case we have seen. Shorten the journey, not the relationship.
bullets: Make the move at the end of Year 10 or in the first term of Year 11

sections.heading: Judging whether the travel is still earning its place
paragraphs: At four weeks, the test is not marks, it is energy. Does your child arrive at the session able to work, or arrive wrung out. Does the tutor start on time, and does the session run its stated length. If the travel is already eroding the lesson at four weeks, it will not improve, because every month after this one is busier than the one before. Alongside that, the ordinary early markers apply: the student can say in a sentence what they are working on, and the tutor has asked to see marked school work.

At one term, look at marks, unevenly. Mathematics and the Sciences generally move first because the gaps are specific and fillable. English and the humanities move over two terms, because what improves is how an answer is built. A term is also the right moment for the radius review. Ask a blunt question: if this tutor lived twenty minutes further away, would we still be doing this. If the answer is no, the arrangement is being held together by convenience rather than by value, and the convenience is about to disappear.

Across a full examination cycle, expect improvement in the subjects worked on, steady grades elsewhere, and a student who handles the final months better than they would have alone. We do not guarantee grades. What tuition reliably improves is the volume of timed past-paper practice, the quality of coursework drafting and how carefully questions are read. Home tuition does not change that arithmetic; it only changes who is doing the travelling. On money, IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai move with the board, the year group, the scarcity of the subject, the length of the session and the distance travelled, which is why there is no sensible price list. Distance is a real input: a tutor giving up ninety minutes of their evening to reach you is pricing that time, so a closer match frequently costs less as well as working better.
bullets: Four weeks: judge energy on arrival, not marks
One term: Sciences and Mathematics first, humanities over two terms
Ask whether you would still do this if the tutor lived further away

sections.heading: Starting IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai with a radius you can keep
paragraphs: Tell us three things and we can set this up properly. The subjects and the year group. The number of minutes a week your family can genuinely give to travel, which is a more useful answer than a pin code. And whether you are planning for this year only or expecting the arrangement to run into Year 11, because those produce different shortlists. A family planning two years should be matched tighter than a family planning two terms, even though the tighter list is shorter. Most families here end up with home tuition as the core arrangement and online held in reserve.

The first session should be diagnostic and unhurried. A good tutor reads the most recent marked school paper, has the student attempt two or three questions aloud, finds out what the school has covered and in what order, and ends by telling you what they think the real problem is and what the first month will target. Have that marked paper ready, along with the school's term calendar if you have it, and ask your child to name two or three topics they would like to stop dreading.

If it stops working, tell us early and tell us why. Pace, communication, subject depth, a personality mismatch or simply a journey that has become unsustainable are all ordinary reasons, and the fifth is the one this page exists for. Raise it at the end of a term rather than in the middle of the examination run, and a replacement is straightforward and usually better than the first match. Raise it in February and we will often advise you to keep the tutor and change the mode instead, which is advice against our own convenience and is still the right advice.
bullets: Send subjects, year group and a weekly travel budget in minutes
Say whether the arrangement needs to survive into Year 11
Have the marked school paper and the term calendar ready

faqs.question: How far should a Year 9 student travel for tuition compared with a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Roughly twice as far, and in practice the gap is wider. What IGCSE tuition near me in Mumbai means changes entirely between the two years. A Year 9 week has slack in it, so a thirty-minute trip each way is absorbed without real cost. By the second half of Year 11, with school running later and mocks and coursework overlapping, the same trip takes a revision session out of every week. Work in minutes rather than kilometres, count both directions, and set the Year 11 budget at the point where you would still be comfortable in January rather than the point that feels fine in August.

faqs.question: My tutor is excellent but lives an hour away. Should I change?
faqs.answer: Change the mode, not the person, if you are already in Year 11. A tutor who understands how your child thinks is worth more than the forty minutes you would save, and a replacement costs about a month of settling at exactly the time you cannot spare it. Ask your current tutor to move some or all sessions online and keep the relationship. If you are still in Year 10, the arithmetic reverses: make the move now, in the cheap part of the year, and it will have repaid itself by the mocks.

faqs.question: Why does a tutor who agreed to travel in June become unreliable by November?
faqs.answer: Because their diary filled up and your slot became the most expensive hour in it. In June a good tutor with free evenings will cross three suburbs without hesitation. By November they have students closer, and the long trip is the one that gets rescheduled when anything goes wrong. This is rarely dishonesty and almost never discussed openly; it shows up as later start times and the occasional cancelled week. If your arrangement relies on an unusually long journey, treat it as fragile from the second term and plan the alternative early.

faqs.question: When is the right month to shorten the journey?
faqs.answer: At the end of Year 10, or during the first term of Year 11 at the latest. A tutor change costs roughly a month of settling and diagnosis. Spent in June or August, that month is cheap and the travel saved over the following terms repays it comfortably. Spent in January, the same month comes out of mock preparation and final coursework, and nothing you save on travel between January and the papers will make it back. Treat the end of the first Year 11 term as the deadline for any change of person.

faqs.question: Is it worth travelling across Mumbai for a better tutor?
faqs.answer: Sometimes in Year 9, rarely in Year 11. A genuinely scarce subject, say a less common language or a specialised Pearson Edexcel option, can justify a long trip while the week still has room. For mainstream subjects the stronger distant tutor usually loses to the adequate close one over a full year, because the close one is still turning up in March. The exception is online, which removes the question entirely. If the tutor you want is in Kandivali East and you are in Chembur, the sensible answer is usually a screen rather than a car.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need access arranged at our building for a weekly slot?
faqs.answer: Yes, and arranging it once removes a recurring problem. Tell your society office the tutor's name and the standing day and time so they are logged as a regular visitor, and give the tutor the wing or tower along with the flat number. In large complexes across Powai, Kharghar and along Ghodbunder Road in Thane, ten minutes can disappear at the entrance otherwise. It matters more as the year tightens, because in Year 11 those ten minutes come out of the lesson rather than out of spare time.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be home, and what should the room have?
faqs.answer: Be present for the first session and the start of the second, then a quiet room is enough for home tuition to work. The room needs a table that fits an A4 past paper flat beside an exercise book, two chairs, decent light and a plug point. Use a common area rather than a bedroom where you can. For a student who has just come off a long school day and a journey, the gap between a prepared table and a cluttered one is about ten minutes of a session, which over a term is a meaningful amount of teaching.

faqs.question: Which parts of Mumbai can you cover for tuition?
faqs.answer: All six zones, matched within each wherever supply allows. South Mumbai from Cuffe Parade and Fort through Babulnath, Walkeshwar and Tardeo. The Western Suburbs from Bandra, Khar West and Juhu out to Malad, Kandivali East and Dahisar East. The Central Suburbs across Powai, Chandivali, Ghatkopar and Kurla. The Eastern Suburbs through Chembur, Wadala, Bhandup and Mulund. Navi Mumbai across Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel. Thane from the station along Pokhran Road and Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali. Cross-zone matches are possible and are the first thing to review each term.

faqs.question: Who is the best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: The question has no answer and the useful version is different. Ask who is a good fit for your child's subjects and level, and who can sustain the journey to you through February. The second half of that sentence rules out more candidates than the first, and it is the half most families ignore until it is too late to act on. A strong tutor your child loses in January has delivered less than a solid one who is still arriving on time during study leave.

faqs.question: Can we switch a long-distance tutor to online and keep everything else the same?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and it is the best outcome available in the final year. The relationship, the subject knowledge and the understanding of your child all survive the switch; only the commute disappears. Make the change at a term boundary rather than mid-topic, agree the same day and time so the habit holds, and make sure your child has a quiet place and a proper screen rather than a phone. An IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai working with a student they already taught in person is a very different proposition from a stranger online.

faqs.question: What does tuition cost and does distance really change it?
faqs.answer: It does, and visibly. Fees depend on the board, the year group, how scarce the subject is, whether the session is sixty or ninety minutes, and how far the tutor travels, because travel is time out of their evening and they price it. A tutor matched within your node in Navi Mumbai or within your stretch of the Western Suburbs usually quotes below one crossing the city for the same lesson. That is one more reason the close match tends to win over a full year: it is often cheaper as well as more durable.

faqs.question: Will moving tuition closer improve my child's grade?
faqs.answer: It improves the conditions, which is not the same thing, and we do not guarantee grades. What a shorter journey reliably buys is a student who arrives able to concentrate, sessions that run their full length, and an arrangement that survives into the final term. Those things correlate with results. They are not a promise, and the work still has to be done. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school or examination board named here. Treat anyone describing a specific final result as certain with suspicion.

sections.heading: How does a mock script turn into an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Send us four things: the subject, the mock grade, the marked script if the school has returned it, and the one weekday evening you can genuinely hold free every week. Within a working day or two you get two or three names, each of whom has taught that board at this level and can reach your building at that hour. Nothing is booked until you have spoken to them.

The script is the part most families leave out, and it is the part that changes the shortlist. A 5 in International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) Chemistry that came from losing almost every mark on the structured six-mark questions needs a different tutor from a 5 built out of steady part-marks and two blank pages at the end. The first is a writing and technique problem. The second is a pace problem, and sometimes a coverage problem, because the department had not finished organic chemistry when it set the paper. We ask which it was before we send names, because the two tutor profiles barely overlap.

Location is the second filter and it is not a soft one. A tutor who has to cross the Western Express Highway at 6pm to reach Khar West from Mulund will be late in week three and gone by week seven. We match along a line or inside a node: Bandra to Santacruz on the Western Line, Ghatkopar to Mulund on the Central Line, Vashi to Nerul inside Navi Mumbai. Searching for IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai is a distance question before it is a quality question, and the distance question is the one that decides whether the sessions are still running in February.
The numbered version, because parents ask for it, runs like this and we do not skip steps when the mock result has made everyone anxious.
bullets: 1. Tell us the subject, the mock grade and the marked script if available
2. We shortlist two or three tutors who have taught that board and paper
3. You speak to them before booking, and compare how each reads the script
4. Confirm a fixed weekly slot that survives the evening peak in your area
5. If the fit is wrong by week three, say so and we re-match

sections.heading: Core or Extended, and what a Mumbai mock grade proves about the tier
paragraphs: A mock grade on its own does not settle the tier question, because the mock was set by the school and not by the board. A Core paper caps the grade no matter how well it is written, and an Extended paper can hand back a low grade to a student who knows the material perfectly well but ran out of time on the last two questions.

This matters in January, when tier entries are being confirmed across Mumbai schools. The IGCSE is offered here mainly through Cambridge International Education and Pearson Edexcel, and in Maths and the sciences the paper your child sat in the mock may not be the paper they will sit in the final series. Ask the subject teacher one specific question: was this mock set at the tier we intend to enter, and if not, what would this script have scored on the other one? A department that pitched its mock high to stretch a comfortable cohort produces grades that frighten parents who were never told that was the plan.

The same logic runs through the International Baccalaureate (IB) side of the house, where a Middle Years Programme (MYP) report or a Diploma Programme (DP) mock sits on criteria rather than a single percentage, and a Higher Level (HL) mock marked to full grade boundaries in October means something quite different from one marked kindly. Families moving a child from IGCSE into the DP often read the two systems with the same eyes, which is a mistake. We keep a panel covering all IB and IGCSE subjects at IGCSE Years 9-11 so a tutor Mumbai parents meet in January can stay with the subject through the final papers and, if the child continues, into DP1.
A tier decision needs more than the number on the front of the script, and most of what it needs is obtainable in one conversation with the department before entries close.
bullets: Whether the mock paper matched the tier the school intends to enter

sections.heading: Reading a mock script paper by paper, subject by subject
paragraphs: The grade is a sum. The script is the evidence. Open the paper and the useful information sits in four places: the questions left blank, the point where the handwriting starts to deteriorate, the questions where the method was right and the final answer wrong, and the topic that failed twice in two different questions. Not one of those four things is visible from the grade.

In IGCSE Maths, a student who loses marks evenly across every topic has a coverage problem, while a student who loses them only in the last twenty-five minutes has a pace problem and the fix is timed sections rather than re-teaching. In Physics and Chemistry the structured questions worth four to six marks are where technique shows: a student who writes correct physics in the wrong order on a describe-and-explain question is not weak at Physics. In English Language, a mock that collapses on the directed writing task and holds up on the reading questions tells you the reading is fine and the problem is form. In Business Studies and Economics the application mark is usually the one missing, because the student answered the textbook question rather than the one about the case study printed in front of them.

Across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai sees the same shape every mock season: the content is more present than the grade suggests, and the marks are leaking somewhere specific. That is why we ask for the script. Internal assessments add a second layer on the IB side, where the Internal Assessment (IA) is marked against criteria rather than a mark scheme, and a mock exam says nothing at all about how an IA is going. Those are two separate conversations and they need two separate pieces of work booked separately.
A first session spent on a returned script usually ends with a written list that looks something like the one below, and the list is more useful to you than any report on the child's attitude.

sections.heading: IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai: where mock season bites hardest
paragraphs: Mock season falls in roughly the same fortnight across Mumbai, Maharashtra, which means every family wants the same Tuesday evening in the same two weeks. Where you live decides how many tutors can realistically hold that slot once the roads thicken.

In South Mumbai the distances are short and the clock is not: a tutor coming from Worli to Colaba covers a few kilometres and can still lose most of an hour at the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak, so we match inside the island rather than bringing someone down from the suburbs over the Bandra-Worli Sea Link. Cuffe Parade, Walkeshwar, Babulnath, Fort and Tardeo sit a short Metro Line 3 or Coastal Road hop from one another, and that is the real catchment. The Western Suburbs run north to south along the Western Line and the Western Express Highway, so Khar West to Santacruz or Malad to Kandivali works and Bandra to Dahisar does not. Juhu, Andheri, Goregaon East, Borivali and Oshiwara are now served by Metro Lines 1, 2A and 7, which has made east-west matching across Andheri far more practical than it used to be.

The Central Suburbs sit on the Central Line and the Eastern Express Highway, with Powai and Chandivali hanging off the Jogeshwari-Vikhroli Link Road (JVLR) in between. Powai has no station of its own, so tutors reach it by road from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar, and a Powai family booking a 7pm slot should expect the tutor to leave home before six. Kurla and Mulund are easier. In the Eastern Suburbs, Chembur, Govandi, Vikhroli, Bhandup and Wadala are tied together by the Central and Harbour lines, the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR) and the Eastern Freeway, and the Freeway makes a Chembur tutor genuinely available to a Wadala family on a weeknight.

The Atal Setu and the Trans-Harbour Line have shortened the crossing, but pulling a tutor over the water for a standing weekday lesson still rarely survives a full term. sections.heading: Why January mocks land differently at Mumbai schools
paragraphs: Schools set mocks for different reasons and they do not announce which reason applies. Some pitch the paper deliberately hard to frighten a comfortable cohort into working. Some pitch it to encourage a group that has lost its nerve. Some simply hand out a past paper in November before the course is finished, which guarantees that a slice of the marks was unteachable on the day. The same percentage means three different things in those three schools, and nobody writes that on the result slip.

Across Mumbai, families at Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, Bombay International School at Babulnath, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade and Activity High School on Peddar Road are working to one calendar, while Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, Utpal Shanghvi Global School and the Billabong High International School campuses run their own. In the Central and Eastern Suburbs, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West and the JBCN International School campuses at Chembur and Parel set their mocks on their own timetables. Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, Navi Mumbai, are a different calendar again. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of these schools, nor with Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. We name them because their calendars are what set the pressure points for the families who use us.

The pressure points themselves are predictable even when the papers are not. October and November bring the first full mock in most Mumbai schools. January brings the second one, and that is the mock that feeds predicted grades. February is coursework and practical assessment. March into April is revision with no new teaching, when a timetable gap is expensive because there is nothing left to catch up on. A Year 11 student in Ghatkopar with an English coursework deadline and a Chemistry practical in the same fortnight as the January mock results is not lazy if the revision slipped that week.

The conversation with the subject teacher is worth preparing. Do not open with the grade, because that turns it into a negotiation. Ask what the paper was set to do, which topics on it had not yet been taught, and what the student would need to change to move this script up one band. That last one is the question most worth asking, because it is the only one whose answer is something you can act on this week.

sections.heading: Should post-mock help be home tuition or online in Mumbai?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the stronger option in the weeks straight after a mock, because the work is physical: the marked script flat on the table, the student's own handwriting, a pen going through it question by question. Online works well once that first diagnostic pass is done, and hybrid is where most Mumbai families end up by March without having planned it.

A home tutor sees things a screen hides. Whether the student reaches for the calculator before finishing the question. Whether the diagram gets drawn at all or only thought about. Whether the last page was rushed because of time or because of dread. IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai also solves a logistics problem that matters more than it sounds: nobody in the family has to travel at 7pm, and the session still happens on an evening when the Eastern Express Highway has stopped moving. The cost is travel time built into the tutor's week, which genuinely narrows the pool to people who can reach you.

An IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai is the right answer in three situations: the subject is scarce and the nearest specialist sits in another zone, the family travels, or the only workable slot is early morning before school. A document camera, or a phone propped over the script, recovers most of what the screen loses. For a Panvel or Kasarvadavali family chasing a particular Computer Science or Economics specialist, online is not the compromise option; it is the only arrangement that will still be running in April. A panel that covers all IB and IGCSE subjects runs home classes Mumbai families book for the main subject alongside online sessions for the scarce second one.

An IGCSE private tutor Mumbai families engage one-to-one will get through the script faster than a group will, but a small group is not automatically worse for revision drill. Judge it on what the mock actually showed. A technique problem is one-to-one work because it needs somebody watching the pen. A coverage problem can be done in a pair, and two students arguing about a mark scheme often learn the command words faster than one student being told them.

sections.heading: What to check yourself about a tutor in Mumbai before February
paragraphs: We check identity, qualifications and board teaching experience before a tutor is listed, and we confirm that the subject and level on the profile is what the person has actually taught rather than what they are willing to attempt. What we cannot check is whether they will suit your particular child. That is what the first session is for, and it is why we re-match without an argument.

What you should check yourself takes about ten minutes and happens in the first conversation. Ask which board they have taught and for how many cohorts, in their own words. Then ask them to look at the mock script with you and say one specific thing about it. A tutor who can say that six marks went on command words and almost nothing went on content is reading the paper. A tutor who says they will revise the whole syllabus from the beginning is reading the grade. The IGCSE tutor Mumbai parents should want in February is the one who narrows the problem, not the one who widens it.

Ask about the gap between now and the final papers. Ask what the first four sessions will cover and how you will know it is working. Ask what they do when a student says the homework is done and it is not, because that situation arrives in most tuition arrangements eventually. Those three answers tell you more than a curriculum vitae does. We do not guarantee grades and no honest tutor will either; what a good one will commit to is that you will know within a month whether the approach is working.

Verification has a practical side in Mumbai housing too. Societies in Powai, Hiranandani Gardens, Kharghar and Thane increasingly want a one-time visitor registration before they will wave through a standing weekly slot, and some ask for police verification paperwork for recurring service visitors. Getting that done in week one is worth the twenty minutes. The alternative is the tutor standing at the gate on a wet Tuesday in July while somebody upstairs looks for the right app.

sections.heading: What is a mock grade actually evidence of?
paragraphs: A mock grade is evidence of how one student performed on one paper, set and marked by their own school, on a date that school chose, against a syllabus that may not have been finished. It is not a board result and it is not a prediction. It is a sample taken early, under conditions nobody outside the school standardised.

Families misread it in both directions, and the comfortable misreading is the more expensive one. A disappointing mock in January is usually good news, because it is the last cheap warning a student gets. Nothing is on a certificate. There are months of teaching left. The student has just been shown, in their own handwriting, exactly where the marks go missing, and there is time to do something about every item on that list. A family that acts on a bad January mock has bought real information at a low price, which is not a thing that happens often in a school year.

A comfortable mock is the result that quietly does damage. It arrives, the house relaxes, and the student stops working with months still to run. The paper may have been pitched to encourage. It may have covered only the portion of the syllabus taught by November, with the hardest material still ahead. It may have been marked generously because the department wanted the cohort to walk into the second term believing in itself. None of those are wrong things for a school to do, but all of them make a good mock grade weaker evidence than a bad one. The question to ask about a comfortable mock is not how pleased to be; it is which topics were not on the paper.

What to extract from a mock is not the grade but the pattern. Which questions were left blank. Where in the paper the time ran out. Which marks were lost to technique rather than knowledge. Whether the same topic failed twice in two different places. A grade is one number and it compresses all four of those into noise. The script is where the information lives, and that is why a tutor's first session after a mock should be spent working through the student's own paper rather than re-teaching the topic from the beginning. Re-teaching assumes the content is missing. In most scripts some of it is and some of it is not, and only the script says which.

Predicted grades drawn from mocks are a judgement rather than a forecast. The teacher is weighing the mock against classwork, coursework and what they know about how this particular student behaves in an exam hall, and two reasonable teachers can read the same script and land in different places. Treat a predicted grade as the school's current reading of your child, which is exactly what it is, and ask what would change it.

The same percentage means different things at different Mumbai schools

sections.heading: How far can a student realistically move between the mock and the final papers?
paragraphs: The honest answer is that it depends almost entirely on what kind of gap it is. A gap made of technique, timing, command words and unattempted questions can close quickly, because the knowledge is already in the student and they are only failing to convert it into marks. A gap made of two years of missing foundations in Maths, or a language the student cannot yet write in under pressure, does not close in a term, and anyone who promises otherwise is selling something.

Movement on a sensible schedule looks roughly like this. By week four, the blank questions stop being blank and the student finishes the paper, even if the last answers are thin. By the end of a term, the topic that failed twice in the mock holds up in a timed question, and the marks that were going on units and command words have largely stopped going. Over a full exam cycle, the pace is stable and the student is spending their last ten minutes on the harder end of the paper rather than surviving the easy end. Those are the markers we would look for. We do not guarantee grades, and anybody who does is guessing on your behalf.

The things that do not move are worth naming too. A student who will not do written practice between sessions. A subject chosen for the wrong reason and genuinely disliked. A timetable with six subjects all in crisis at once. The third is common in Mumbai in January and the only useful response is triage: pick the two subjects where the marks are most recoverable, do those properly, and hold the rest steady with school support. Trying to fix six at once generally fixes none of them and exhausts the student by March.

If it is not working, say so early. A fit problem shows up by week three, not week ten, and the signs are consistent across families: the student goes quiet about the sessions, the homework stops getting done, the tutor's updates get vaguer. Tell us and we re-match. There is no argument and no penalty. A tutor who is wrong for one child is frequently right for another, and we would far rather move quickly than have a family sit through six weeks of politeness while the calendar runs down.
bullets: Week four: the paper gets finished and blank questions stop appearing
One term: the twice-failed topic holds up under timed conditions

sections.heading: Booking a first session around your child's marked mock paper
paragraphs: Bring three things to the first session: the marked script, the mark scheme if the school released it, and the student. If the school has not returned the script, ask for it. Most will, and the session is worth considerably more with it in the room. If it genuinely cannot leave the building, bring the question paper and the student's own account of which questions went badly, which is a poorer source but not a useless one.

The first session is diagnostic and it should feel like it. The tutor goes through the paper with the student, question by question, asking what happened at each lost mark rather than explaining the topic again. By the end there should be a short written list: the topics that need re-teaching, the techniques that need drilling, and a timing target for the next full paper. That list is the plan, and you should be shown it rather than told the session went well.

IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on the board, the level, how scarce the subject specialist is, how far the tutor travels to your building and how long each session runs. A Chemistry tutor working inside Bandra and a Further Maths specialist travelling out to Kharghar are not the same arrangement and they are not the same cost. We will give you the range for your specific request when we send the shortlist, rather than publishing a figure that would be wrong for most of the people reading it.

A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families can call on is not one person; it is a panel, and the right one for your child is chosen on the evidence sitting in that script. Send it to us and the matching gets considerably more accurate.

faqs.question: Is a disappointing mock grade in January a reason to panic?
faqs.answer: No, and it is usually the most useful result your child will get all year. A January mock is the last cheap warning available: nothing is on a certificate, there are months of teaching left, and the script shows exactly where the marks went. Panic wastes the window. What works is reading the paper properly within a week, picking the two or three recoverable problems, and starting on them. The families who struggle later are more often the ones who got a comfortable mock in January and stopped working than the ones who got a bad one and reacted to it.

faqs.question: My child did well in the mock. Is tuition still worth considering?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the first question to ask is which parts of the syllabus were not on that paper. Schools often set a mock in November or December covering only the material taught so far, with the harder content still ahead. A comfortable mock can also be deliberately pitched to encourage a cohort. Neither makes the grade dishonest, but both make it weaker evidence than a low one. Ask the subject teacher what the paper covered and what it was marked against. If the answer is the full syllabus at full boundaries, relax a little. If not, the grade is a partial picture of a partial course.

faqs.question: Should we ask the school to return the marked mock script?
faqs.answer: Yes, and ask early, because the script is worth far more than the grade. The marked paper shows which questions were skipped, where the answers got shorter, which marks went to method errors and which topic failed twice. None of that is visible from a percentage. Most Mumbai schools return scripts or let parents see them at a meeting; some keep them because the paper will be reused with the next cohort. If it cannot leave the school, photograph it at the meeting or ask the teacher to list the lost marks by question number. A tutor working from the script does better work in session one.

faqs.question: How reliable is a predicted grade based on the mock?
faqs.answer: A predicted grade is a teacher's judgement rather than a forecast, and it is built from more than the mock. The teacher weighs classwork, coursework, effort and what they know about how this student behaves in an exam hall. Two reasonable teachers can read the same script and predict differently, which is not a failure of either of them. Treat it as the school's current reading of your child and ask what would change it. That question is far more useful than arguing about the number, because the answer tells you what the department is actually watching between now and the final papers.

faqs.question: Will a tutor really travel to our building in Thane on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor already lives or works on your side of Thane. Ghodbunder Road sets the schedule: a tutor near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening peak, so we match within the corridor rather than across it. A Pokhran Road or Majiwada family has a wider pool to draw on than a Kasarvadavali one. Tell us your exact locality and the time you want, not just the word Thane, and we will only send tutors who can hold that slot in February as reliably as they could in October.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but an adult should be in the flat. That is standard practice for home tuition and it protects both the student and the tutor. Beyond that, the useful thing a parent can do is be available for five minutes at the end of the first few sessions to hear what the tutor found in the script. On space: a dining table in a room with a door that closes beats a bedroom, and a bedroom beats a hall with the television on. The tutor needs a hard surface, decent light and nobody walking through every ten minutes.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE tuition in Mumbai cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on five things, and we will not publish a figure that would be wrong for most readers. The board, the level, how scarce the subject specialist is, how far the tutor travels to your building and how long each session runs all move it. A Chemistry tutor working inside Bandra and a Further Maths specialist travelling to Kharghar are not comparable. Session length matters more than parents expect, because ninety minutes on a mock script does roughly twice the work of a rushed hour. Send us the subject, level and locality and we will quote a range alongside the shortlist.

faqs.question: Can a tutor get into our society in Powai without a problem every week?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, once the visit is registered properly. Most larger complexes in Powai, Hiranandani Gardens, Kharghar and Thane now run app-based visitor passes or a one-time registration for recurring service visits. Do it in week one: give the tutor's name and number to the gate as a standing weekly entry and the problem disappears for the rest of the term. Skip it and you get the tutor stuck downstairs on the one evening the lift is also out. If your society requires police verification paperwork for recurring visitors, tell us before we match so we can factor it into the shortlist.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for going through a marked mock paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one condition: the tutor has to be able to see the page rather than the student's face. A phone propped over the script or an inexpensive document camera recovers most of what a screen loses, and annotating a scanned paper on a shared screen works well for structured questions. What online does less well is catching physical habits, such as whether the diagram gets drawn or whether the calculator comes out before the question is read. For a Panvel or Kasarvadavali family chasing a scarce specialist, online is not a compromise; it is the arrangement that will still be running in April.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we re-match, with no argument and no penalty. A fit problem is usually visible by week three: the student goes quiet about the sessions, the homework stops, the tutor's updates get vaguer. Say so then rather than at week ten, when there is less runway. We will ask two questions, what specifically is not working and what you would want different, and use the answers to choose the next tutor rather than sending a random replacement. A tutor who is wrong for one child is often right for another, so this is a matching problem and not a verdict on anyone.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we add tuition in after a bad mock?
faqs.answer: Two, usually, and three at the outside. A Year 11 student in January already has school, coursework and revision; adding four tutors produces a timetable nobody can keep and homework that gets done badly for everybody. Look at the scripts and pick the subjects where the marks are most recoverable, which generally means the ones where technique and timing are the problem rather than two years of missing foundations. Hold the others steady with school support and a weekend past paper. Families who triage in January tend to see more movement than families who try to repair everything at once.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram connected to my child's school or to the exam board?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any school, nor with Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. We name schools on this page only because their calendars and mock timetables shape the pressure points for the families who use us, and nothing here should be read as an endorsement by any of them. Tutors are matched on board and subject experience, not on any school relationship. We also do not guarantee grades. What we can do is put a specialist in front of your child's own script quickly, while the result is still fresh enough to act on.

sections.heading: How does IB Gram match an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai to a specific gap?
paragraphs: IB Gram starts from the gap, not the subject. You tell us the board, the examination year printed on the school's entry letter, the paper that went wrong and the topic the subject teacher flagged. We then shortlist people who have taught that exact paper at that exact tier, and send two or three profiles with the reasoning attached. The honest answer to IGCSE tutor cost in Mumbai is that it follows from what the shortlist has to contain, which is why the request gets written down in detail before anyone is approached.

Most enquiries arrive with a symptom rather than a diagnosis. A mother in Chembur says her son has gone from comfortable to lost in Chemistry; a father in Kandivali East says the Maths marks dropped after the Christmas assessment. Neither statement tells a tutor what to teach on Tuesday. So the first conversation is spent turning the symptom into something examinable: which question types lose marks, whether the loss is content, method or reading the question, and whether the same weakness appeared in last year's report and was waved through. IB Gram works across all IB and IGCSE subjects a home tutor in Mumbai is ever asked for, so the written request is what narrows the search rather than the subject label alone.
