sections.heading: Starting IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai: what to have ready
paragraphs: Three things make the first session useful. The most recent marked school paper, with the teacher's comments still on it. The school's term calendar, or whatever part of it you have, including internal test weeks and coursework dates. And a short list from your child, not from you, of the two or three topics they would most like to stop being bad at. That last item changes the tone of the first hour more than anything else, because it makes the student a participant rather than a subject.

The first session itself should be diagnostic and it should feel slightly slow. A good tutor spends it reading the marked paper, asking your child to attempt two or three questions aloud, and finding out what the school has already covered and in what order. They should end it by telling you, in plain terms, what they think the actual problem is and what the first month will target. If they end it by telling you everything is fine and they will start the syllabus from the beginning, ask why.

If the match is not working, say so early and say so to us rather than only to the tutor. A replacement is straightforward: tell us what specifically is not working, whether it is pace, communication, subject depth or simply that the two of them do not get on, and we match again using that information, which makes the second match better than the first. Most replacements happen because of fit rather than competence, and there is no awkwardness in it. We would far rather change a tutor in week five than discover in February that nothing has moved since October.
bullets: Bring the most recent marked school paper with comments intact
Have the school term calendar and internal test weeks to hand
Ask your child for their own list of two or three problem topics
Expect a slow diagnostic first session that ends with a stated plan
Report a poor fit in week five, not in February

faqs.question: Why match by school instead of by distance?
faqs.answer: Because the school sets the deadlines, and the deadlines are what tutoring has to work around. A tutor already teaching another student at your child's school knows the internal submission calendar, the department's marking habits and which teacher sets what, so the plan is right in week one rather than week four. Mumbai's IGCSE schools cluster tightly in places like Bandra Kurla Complex, Juhu and Powai, which means a school-matched tutor is usually close by anyway. Distance is a constraint worth checking second, not the filter worth searching with first, so treat an IGCSE tutor near me in Mumbai as shorthand for the right school rather than the shortest drive.

faqs.question: What if no tutor currently teaches at my child's school?
faqs.answer: Then we widen to the cluster, which is the next best thing and works well. Most Mumbai international schools sit within a few kilometres of three or four others running the same board and a similar term structure, so a tutor from Jamnabai Narsee International School's pool knows roughly what Ecole Mondiale World School is doing in the same month. A cluster tutor needs about three weeks to learn your school's specific internal calendar instead of knowing it on day one. Tell them the mock dates and the coursework deadlines at the first session and that gap closes quickly.

faqs.question: Can I ask the tutor what they think of my child's class teacher?
faqs.answer: Please do not. A tutor who works inside that school every week has an obvious conflict of interest, and answering honestly could cost them other families. It is an unfair question even when they are willing to answer it. Ask instead what the mark scheme rewards, how the department expects working to be presented, and whether the internal tests are harder than the real papers. Those questions get you the same practical information with none of the awkwardness, and the answers are actually more useful because they are about the assessment rather than about a person.

faqs.question: Is there a downside to a tutor who is embedded in one school?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth knowing. A tutor teaching several students at one school absorbs that school's assumptions about which topics matter and how answers should look. Usually that is exactly what you want. Occasionally the school's own approach is the thing holding your child back, and an embedded tutor is the least likely person to notice. If your child has been told repeatedly by the school that they are a Core candidate and you disagree, a tutor from outside that building may give you a cleaner second opinion on whether the Extended route is realistic.

faqs.question: Do you cover Navi Mumbai and Thane, or only the island and the Western Suburbs?
faqs.answer: Both, with separate tutor pools. Navi Mumbai works node to node, so a Nerul or Belapur tutor covers Vashi, Kharghar and Panvel along Palm Beach Road, and families near D.Y. Patil International School are usually matched within the node. Thane has its own pool running from the station out along Pokhran Road and Ghodbunder Road to Kasarvadavali and Hiranandani Estate. Pulling a tutor across the creek or down the Eastern Express Highway for a weekday evening rarely survives a full term, which is why we match inside the zone wherever supply allows.

faqs.question: How does a tutor get into our society for a weekly home session?
faqs.answer: Most Mumbai complexes need the tutor registered as a regular visitor rather than cleared at the gate each week. Speak to your society office once, give them the tutor's name and the standing day and time, and the weekly friction disappears. For an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai arriving at the same hour every week, that single conversation matters more than it sounds. Also tell the tutor the tower number and the lift they need, because large complexes in Powai, Kharghar and Thane are easy to get lost in and ten minutes lost at the gate is ten minutes off the lesson.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but be there for the first one and for the first twenty minutes of the second. You are checking the things we cannot check for you: whether the tutor asks your child questions or lectures them, whether they ask to see school materials, and whether your child talks. After that, a quiet room with a table, a plug point and the door open is enough. Avoid the bedroom if there is any alternative. A dining table in a semi-public part of the flat works better for concentration and for everyone's comfort.

faqs.question: What happens if a session is missed because of traffic or rain?
faqs.answer: Agree the rule in the first week and the problem never becomes an argument. The standard arrangement is that a session cancelled by the family with reasonable notice is rescheduled, and a session the tutor cannot reach is made up. Mumbai makes this real: a heavy monsoon evening on the Western Express Highway or Ghodbunder Road can take a tutor out for the day. Many families keep a fallback online slot for exactly these evenings, which costs nothing to set up and saves a week of lost momentum during the monsoon months.

faqs.question: Who is the best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai?
faqs.answer: There is no such person, and anyone who answers that question is selling something. The useful question is who is the right tutor for a Year 11 student at your specific school doing your specific subjects at Extended level. That has a real answer and it changes by subject, by school and by year group. A tutor who transforms a Year 10 Chemistry student may be the wrong fit for the same family's Year 11 English Literature. Ask for the right match rather than the best name, and judge it at four weeks.

faqs.question: What does tutoring cost, and why will nobody quote a figure?
faqs.answer: Because the honest answer is a range and the factors are knowable. Rates move with the board, the year group, how scarce the subject is, how far the tutor travels, and whether the session is sixty or ninety minutes. A Year 11 Extended Physics tutor travelling to Cuffe Parade on a weekday evening costs more than a Year 9 Mathematics tutor working two buildings away in Kandivali East. Ask for a figure for your exact combination and you will get one. A price list published without those variables would be wrong for almost every family reading it.

faqs.question: Can a tutor cover more than one subject for the same student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking. Mathematics and Physics pair naturally, as do Chemistry and Biology, and a single tutor across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai is realistically strong in keeps the week simpler and the travel lower. Beyond two closely related subjects, be sceptical. Someone claiming genuine Extended-level depth in Mathematics, Chemistry, Economics and English Literature at once is unlikely, and the thin subject is usually the one your child needs most. Two tutors on two evenings is often the better arrangement despite the extra coordination.

faqs.question: Will tutoring guarantee a better IGCSE grade?
faqs.answer: No, and we do not guarantee grades. What good tutoring reliably changes is the quality of preparation: more past papers attempted under timed conditions, better reading of what a question is asking, cleaner presentation of working, and coursework submitted on a plan rather than in a panic. Those things correlate strongly with results but they are not a promise, and the student still has to do the work. sections.heading: How IB Gram matches an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai to a tiering problem
paragraphs: A tiering enquiry almost never arrives described as one. A parent writes that Maths has gone from fine to difficult over two terms, or that the Chemistry teacher has started using the word Core in parents' evening conversations, or that the Year 10 report carried a comment nobody in the family quite understood. What the household actually needs is someone who can read the last two years of marks and say, with reasons on paper, whether the harder tier is reachable from where the student currently stands. That is a much narrower brief than general subject help, and the match has to reflect it or the first month is wasted.

So the first thing IB Gram asks for is evidence rather than a subject name. With that in hand we look for a tutor who has taught both tiers of that subject, not only the harder one. A tutor whose entire experience is Extended candidates tends to treat the Extended paper as the obvious destination, and that is precisely the assumption a worried family needs tested rather than confirmed.

Matching is then geographic, because a tier case runs for months and a weekly slot that depends on crossing the city at 6pm will not survive a full term. sections.heading: What are Core and Extended tiers, and why does the choice cap a grade?
paragraphs: Several IGCSE subjects are examined at two tiers. Cambridge International Education calls them Core and Extended. Pearson Edexcel calls its equivalent split Foundation and Higher. The two tiers sit different question papers on the same subject, and each tier carries its own range of available grades. A student entered for the lower tier cannot be awarded the top grades, however well they perform on the day.

This is the part families miss. Tiering is not a ranking of sets inside the school and it is not a prediction written in a report. It is an entry decision that the school submits to the board, and it changes which paper physically arrives in the exam hall. On Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics the Core candidate sits one set of papers and the Extended candidate sits another, with a longer and harder syllabus content list behind it. The published grade range for the Core tier stops below the top grades, while the Extended range runs up to A*. Check the current syllabus for the session your child will actually sit, because Cambridge revises specifications and the detail of what each tier covers does move between cycles.

The Middle Years Programme (MYP) does not work this way at all, which is why families moving from an International Baccalaureate (IB) MYP school into an IGCSE cohort are so often blindsided. MYP reports against published criteria on an eight-point scale, with no tiering anywhere in the structure and no moment where a paper is chosen for a student. IGCSE asks the school to commit, on a form, to one paper per tiered subject. A parent who has spent three years reading criterion descriptors has no instinct at all for an entry deadline, and nothing in the MYP reporting cycle teaches them to look for one.

The second thing to understand is that the cap is set before the exam, not discovered after it. By the time results arrive, the decision that limited them is a year old and entirely unarguable. Everything useful happens in the window between the first serious Year 10 assessments and the school's entry submission, and that window is where IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai is genuinely worth paying for. Outside it, a tutor can improve a grade within a range. Inside it, a tutor can change the range.

sections.heading: Which IGCSE subjects are tiered, and where does it bite hardest?
paragraphs: Mathematics is where tiering matters most, followed by the sciences. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Co-ordinated Sciences all run Core and Extended routes, and so does English as a Second Language. Geography, History, Economics, Business Studies and first-language English carry no tier split at all, which is why a report can flag two subjects and leave the rest untouched.

Mathematics bites hardest because of what sits downstream of it. A Core entry removes the harder content from the syllabus, which means the student never formally meets several topics that later courses assume they have seen. The sciences bite next, because a capped science grade is read closely by anyone deciding whether Higher Level (HL) Chemistry or Physics is a sensible load two years later. English as a Second Language is the quiet one that families overlook entirely: the Core route caps the grade in the same way, and some admissions processes read the certificate line rather than asking which tier produced it.

Within a subject the gap is not evenly spread either, and this changes what a tutor should do. In Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics the Extended content adds whole areas rather than harder versions of the same questions. A student who is comfortable with the Core material and simply slow is a completely different case from a student who has never been taught the extra content at all, and the two need different work from the first hour. The first needs timing, accuracy and question-reading discipline. The second needs the missing topics taught in order, with enough weeks left on the calendar to actually use them under pressure.

This is the practical reason to book across all IB and IGCSE subjects a tutor in Mumbai can cover inside one household rather than hiring one specialist per subject. Tier flags usually arrive together. A Year 10 student flagged for Core Mathematics is very often flagged for Core Chemistry in the same report, and a single tutor who sees both can tell you whether the problem is the subject itself or the algebra and arithmetic sitting underneath both of them. That distinction decides whether you need eight weeks of Maths or eight weeks of Chemistry, and getting it wrong costs the window.

sections.heading: Tier conversations across the six zones of Mumbai
paragraphs: Mumbai, Maharashtra runs Cambridge IGCSE cohorts in every zone of the city, and the tier conversation plays out differently in each one because the schools and the travel differ. In South Mumbai the IGCSE schools sit close together and the families do not: Cuffe Parade, Colaba, Fort, Babulnath, Walkeshwar, Peddar Road, Tardeo and Worli are a few kilometres apart and still forty minutes apart in the evening once the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals load up. Tutors here are matched inside the island, using the Western Line between Churchgate and Mumbai Central, the Harbour Line out of CSMT, Metro Line 3 running from Cuffe Parade towards BKC, and the Coastal Road.

In the Western Suburbs the pattern is linear and unforgiving. Bandra, Khar West, Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri, Goregaon East, Malad, Kandivali, Borivali and Dahisar string along the Western Line, the Western Express Highway and Link Road, with Metro Line 1 running Versova to Ghatkopar and Metro Lines 2A and 7 covering Dahisar down to Gundavali. Matching along that spine works: Khar West to Santacruz, Malad to Kandivali. Matching across it, Juhu to Powai at half past six on a Wednesday, does not, and a tier case needs the same tutor every week for months rather than whoever is free.

The Central Suburbs are Powai, Chandivali, Kurla, Kanjurmarg, Ghatkopar and Andheri East, hung off the Central Line, JVLR and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road (SCLR). Powai is the awkward one because it has no station of its own, so a Powai family's realistic tutor pool is whoever can drive in from Andheri East, Kanjurmarg or Ghatkopar. The Eastern Suburbs run from Chembur and Govandi up through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund on the Central and Harbour lines and the Eastern Express Highway, with the Eastern Freeway and the Chembur to Wadala Monorail putting South Mumbai closer than the map suggests. Parents type IGCSE tutors near me in Mumbai and get results from the whole city. The only ones worth calling are on your side of the Freeway.

Navi Mumbai works in nodes. Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are short drives apart on Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, linked by the Harbour and Trans-Harbour lines and Navi Mumbai Metro Line 1 from Belapur to Pendhar. The Atal Setu has changed what a Navi Mumbai family can reach on a Saturday, but it has not changed a Tuesday at seven, so an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai working with a Kharghar family is still a Navi Mumbai tutor. Thane spreads from the station out along Pokhran Road, Ghodbunder Road and Majiwada to Kasarvadavali, and Ghodbunder sets the timetable: twenty minutes off-peak, close to an hour in the evening peak. Thane tutors cover Thane, and Mulund tutors sometimes cross the Eastern Express Highway to help.

sections.heading: When Mumbai schools decide tiers, and the Year 10 evidence behind it
paragraphs: The school makes the entry decision, not the family and not the tutor. A subject teacher proposes a tier, a head of department or the examinations officer signs it off, and the school submits entries to the board. Most Mumbai schools form a settled view during Year 10 and confirm it early in Year 11, and the evidence they lean on is the student's internal paper marks across that year rather than classwork, effort grades or attitude comments.

What counts as evidence varies by school and it is worth knowing which kind you are dealing with. At schools such as Dhirubhai Ambani International School in BKC, Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade and Bombay International School at Babulnath, the Year 10 end-of-year paper is often sat under tier conditions, so the mark maps directly onto the entry decision and the argument is narrow. Elsewhere, including Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, Bombay Cambridge International School in Andheri East, Thakur International School in Kandivali East, JBCN International School, Chembur, NES International School in Mulund West, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul, the view is assembled from several smaller assessments across the year. Both approaches are reasonable. They are not equally easy to argue with.

The calendar is why families find out late. Year 10 ends, the summer break swallows the conversation entirely, Year 11 starts with mocks already on the horizon, and the entry goes in while everyone is thinking about something else. By the time the first Year 11 report lands on the kitchen table, the tier is frequently already on a form. Mumbai schools running the May exam series work backwards from a submission date in the preceding months, and schools using the October or November series run the identical squeeze earlier in the year. Neither sends a letter saying your window closes now.

We name schools because their calendars set the pressure points families here actually live with. We also do not guarantee grades, and no honest tutor will tell you a tier can always be changed once a form has gone in.

sections.heading: Is home tuition in Mumbai better than online for tier preparation?
paragraphs: For a tier decision, home tuition in Mumbai is usually the better first choice. The work is diagnostic before it is instructional, and a tutor sitting beside a Year 10 student watching how they attack an unfamiliar Extended question learns more in one hour than three weeks of screen-shared worked solutions will ever tell them.

Home tutoring also solves the evidence problem, which matters more here than on an ordinary subject enquiry. The school's file stays at school. The student's own file, the marked papers, the half-finished notebooks, the loose sheet where they stopped halfway and never went back, is at home in a drawer, and a tutor physically in the room gets to see all of it inside the first session. We lead with home tutoring on these enquiries for exactly that reason, and we cover all IB and IGCSE subjects in home classes across Mumbai rather than treating a home visit as a premium add-on to be negotiated.

Online is genuinely the better answer in three situations and we will say so rather than sell you a visit. If the specialism is scarce, an IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai may be the only person available who has actually taught both tiers of Co-ordinated Sciences. If the family is in Kasarvadavali or Panvel and the right tutor lives near Bandra, online keeps a weekly slot alive that travel would kill inside a month. And if the student is in the last stretch before an entry decision and needs three short sessions a week rather than one long one, only online makes that schedule survive the Western Express Highway in December.

Hybrid is where most tier cases land. The diagnostic sessions and the first few weeks of missing content happen at home, then maintenance sessions move online once the tutor knows how that particular student thinks and where they bluff. The honest trade-off is attention: a fourteen-year-old on a laptop in a flat with the television on is a different student from the one at the dining table, and the tutor has less to read. Say so at the start, agree that the camera stays on and that working gets photographed and sent after each session, and hybrid holds for a full term.

sections.heading: How IGCSE tutors are checked before they reach your Mumbai building
paragraphs: Every tutor on IB Gram is identity-verified and has their qualifications and teaching history checked before a profile goes live. For IGCSE work we additionally record which boards and which tiers a tutor has taught, because the two are not interchangeable and the profile is useless to you without it. Having taught Extended Mathematics for years says nothing about whether someone can get a borderline candidate cleanly through the Core papers, which is a different skill with different habits.

What we cannot check is fit, and that part is yours to do on the introduction call. Ask the three questions that separate a subject tutor from a tier tutor. Which tier were your last three IGCSE students entered for, and why. What would make you tell a parent that Extended is the wrong call for their child. How do you present evidence to a school that has already made up its mind. A tutor who answers the second question with some version of Extended is always better has told you everything you need to know in one sentence.

There is no single best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai, and anyone presenting themselves that way for a tiering question is guessing at a problem they have not seen. The right person for a Core-to-Extended push in Physics is not automatically the right person for a student who should be moved down to Core and protected from a paper they cannot reach. An IGCSE private tutor Mumbai families engage for a tier case has to be able to argue the decision in both directions and mean it.

Check these yourself before the first paid session, because they take two minutes each. Photo identity at your door against the profile you were sent. The specific syllabus the tutor says they teach against the one printed on your child's school letter or report. And whether they will put a short written read in your inbox after the diagnostic session. That last one is the real test. A tutor willing to commit a tier opinion to text has thought about it properly, and a tutor who only ever gives verbal reassurance at the door has not.

sections.heading: How do you ask a Mumbai school to change a tier entry?
paragraphs: Bring evidence, not feeling, and bring it early. A school will reconsider a tier on new marks from work done under the harder paper's conditions. It will not reconsider on a parent's confidence in their own child. Ask for a meeting with the subject teacher and the head of department together, and ask for it well before the entry submission closes rather than after someone mentions it in passing.

The evidence that works is boring and specific. A past-style Extended paper done under timed conditions and marked by the tutor, with the raw script attached rather than a summary of it. A topic-by-topic list of what the student could not do eight weeks ago and can demonstrably do now. A record of attendance at the extra sessions, because schools read effort as a proxy for whether the improvement will hold. If the student is being moved down instead, the same evidence works in reverse: an Extended paper attempted honestly, with most of the back half blank, is a far stronger argument for Core than any conversation about stress or confidence.

The deadline is real and it is earlier than parents expect. Once the school has submitted entries to the board, a change becomes an administrative amendment with its own window and sometimes an additional charge, and once that window shuts the tier is simply fixed for the series. Ask the examinations officer, by email so that you have it in writing, for two dates: when the school internally finalises tiers, and the last date the board will accept an amendment. Those two dates define your entire window of influence, and everything a tutor does has to fit inside the first one.

Tone matters more here than people admit, because IGCSE cohorts at Mumbai schools are small and you will be dealing with the same head of department for two more years. Go in asking what would change your mind, rather than asking why my child was put on Core. Schools respond to the first framing and close ranks on the second. On IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai, this is also the one stretch where intensive help is clearly worth the money, because it is the only stretch where the ceiling itself is still movable rather than the mark underneath it.

Then there is the downstream effect, which is the real reason to treat a Mathematics flag in Year 10 as urgent. A capped IGCSE Mathematics grade makes the Diploma Programme (DP) harder Mathematics course a difficult ask two years later. Coordinators look at whether a student has formally met the content that Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes, and a Core certificate states on its face that they have not. The door is not bolted shut, and students do bridge it with summer work and a strong case, but it becomes heavier because of a form signed when the child was fifteen.
bullets: Ask the examinations officer for two dates: internal finalisation and board amendment
Bring a timed Extended script, marked, with the raw paper attached
A mostly blank harder paper is strong evidence for moving down to Core
Ask what would change your mind, not why was my child placed here
A capped Mathematics grade makes Higher Level Analysis and Approaches harder to take

sections.heading: What progress looks like while the entry decision is still open
paragraphs: At four weeks you should have a tier opinion, not a grade change. A competent tutor will have run a diagnostic, taught two or three of the topics the Core route leaves out, re-tested them cold a fortnight later, and told you plainly whether the gap is content, speed or confidence. If nobody has committed to anything definite by week four, that silence is the signal rather than the marks.

At one term the measurable thing is a timed paper at the harder tier, marked properly, placed next to the one from week one. The total may still look low and that is not necessarily a problem. What should have changed is the shape of the script: fewer blanks, more partially-credited working, and the student reaching the final page. A student who now attempts everything and scores moderately is in a materially different position from one who still stops halfway, even when the two totals are close enough to look identical on a report.

Across one exam cycle, the honest set of outcomes is this. Some students move up a tier and justify the move. Some stay exactly where they were and do noticeably better on the paper they were always going to sit, which is a real result and the one families consistently undervalue. And some are moved down on the tutor's own advice and come away with a clean grade instead of a damaged one. IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor can tell you in week one which of those three you are looking at.

On cost, IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai is priced on the board and level, how scarce the subject specialism is, how far the tutor travels and how long each session runs. A tiered science with a tutor who has taught both routes sits above general Year 9 support, simply because fewer people can do it. A tutor crossing the Bandra-Worli Sea Link twice a week prices that time in, and so does a tutor giving up an evening to the Eastern Express Highway. Nobody should quote you a figure before they know the subject, the tier and the area.
bullets: Four weeks: a written tier opinion with reasons, not a grade jump
One term: a timed harder-tier paper compared against week one
Fewer blanks and a finished script matter more than the total
Staying on Core and scoring well is a legitimate good outcome
Fees depend on board, specialism scarcity, travel distance and session length

sections.heading: Starting with an IGCSE home tuition enquiry in Mumbai
paragraphs: Send three things and the shortlist comes back quickly: the subject and board, your area and the evening slot that realistically works, and a photograph of the most recent school report. If the school has written anything at all about tiers, send that too, even if it is a single line in a comment box or a sentence somebody said at a parents' meeting. It is the document that shortens the whole enquiry, because it tells the tutor what they are arguing with.

The first session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson, and it helps to know that in advance so nobody feels short-changed. Expect the tutor to put a short mixed set in front of your child, part Core-level and part Extended-level, and to watch rather than teach. Expect questions directed at you about what the school has said and when it said it. Expect no verdict inside the first hour. A tutor who announces on day one that your child is obviously Extended material has not actually looked at anything yet.

Practically, clear a table and a plug point rather than pointing the tutor at a bedroom desk. Tell the society gate in advance so the tutor is not standing at the entrance of a Kandivali, Chembur or Thane tower while your paid hour runs. Keep the house normal, because a parent hovering changes what the tutor is able to see. We can arrange a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai families need inside one household, which in practice usually means one visit covering Mathematics and a science instead of two tutors on two separate evenings.

If the first tutor is not right, say so after the second session rather than the eighth. Replacement is a message, not a negotiation, and the diagnostic notes and marked scripts transfer across so you are not buying the same first hour twice. That is the main reason to match through a platform rather than through a neighbour's recommendation: when the fit is wrong, you can change it without losing the relationship or the weeks.
bullets: Send subject, board, area, evening slot and the latest school report
First session is diagnostic: mixed Core and Extended questions, no verdict
Clear a table and a plug point, not a bedroom desk
Pre-clear the tutor at your society gate to protect the paid hour
Ask for a replacement after session two, not session eight

faqs.question: What exactly is the difference between Core and Extended at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: They are two different exam papers for the same subject, carrying different ranges of available grades. Cambridge International Education sets a Core route and an Extended route in several IGCSE subjects, and Pearson Edexcel calls its version Foundation and Higher. The Extended route covers additional syllabus content, and the Core route's published grade range stops short of the top grades. The school enters a student for one tier before the exam series begins, which means the ceiling is fixed in advance rather than discovered in the results. Check the current syllabus for the session your child will sit, because specifications are revised between cycles.

faqs.question: Who decides which tier my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: The school does. The subject teacher proposes a tier, the head of department or the examinations officer confirms it, and the school submits entries to the board. Parents are usually consulted and are sometimes only informed after the fact. You can ask for a decision to be reviewed and schools do review them, but the review runs on marks from work done under the harder paper's conditions rather than on a conversation. Ask early which Year 10 assessments the school is treating as tier evidence, so you know what you would be arguing with before anything is written down.

faqs.question: Can we still move from Core to Extended in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the limiting factor is the calendar rather than the rule. Schools internally finalise tiers before submitting entries, and boards allow amendments for a window after that, occasionally with an administrative charge attached. Once that window closes the tier is fixed for the series. The practical question is whether your child can produce a credible timed Extended script before the school's internal deadline, which usually means several weeks of focused work on the content the Core route leaves out. Ask the examinations officer for both dates in writing before you plan anything around it.

faqs.question: Is being entered for Extended always the better option?
faqs.answer: No, and assuming it is causes real damage. A student entered for Extended who cannot access the harder questions can finish with large blank sections and a lower grade than the same student would have earned on the Core paper, where the questions are within reach and the marks are gettable. The honest test is a timed harder-tier paper under exam conditions. If most of the back half is still blank after eight weeks of targeted teaching, Core is the better entry. A clean Core grade reads better on a certificate than a damaged Extended one.

faqs.question: Will a Core Mathematics grade affect Diploma Programme choices two years later?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the harder Mathematics course. Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level assumes content that the Core IGCSE Mathematics route does not formally cover, and Diploma Programme coordinators read a certificate with that in mind. It is not an automatic bar, and students do bridge the gap with summer work and a well-argued case. But it is the single clearest reason to treat a Mathematics tier flag in Year 10 as urgent rather than as something to revisit later. The subject choice conversation at the end of Year 11 is already downstream of a decision made months earlier.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE tuition cost here?
faqs.answer: It depends on four things, and nobody should quote you a number before knowing them: the board and level, how scarce the subject specialism is, how far the tutor travels, and how long each session runs. A tiered science with a tutor who has taught both Core and Extended routes sits above general Year 9 support. Travel is real money in this city, since a tutor crossing from Andheri to Powai in the evening peak is giving up most of an extra hour. Rates for an IGCSE tutor in Mumbai are agreed directly with the tutor before the first session, in writing.

faqs.question: We live in Kharghar. Will a tutor actually come out here on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is already in Navi Mumbai. We match node to node across Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel, because a tutor driving out from the island city over the Atal Setu for a seven o'clock slot will quietly stop coming by the second month. Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway keep Navi Mumbai internally quick, so a Belapur or Nerul tutor holds a Kharghar slot comfortably for a full term. If the specialism you need does not exist locally, we will say so and suggest online rather than promise a crossing nobody can sustain.

faqs.question: Does someone need to be at home during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: An adult should be in the flat, but not in the room. Most Mumbai families have a parent, grandparent or house help present, which is what we ask for and what satisfies most society visitor rules as well. Sitting inside the session changes what the tutor can see, because a fourteen-year-old performs for a parent and will not admit they have forgotten something basic. Stay in the next room, leave the door open if you prefer, and ask for the tutor's read afterwards instead. The first diagnostic session is the exception, where your account of what the school has said is genuinely useful.

faqs.question: Our building has strict gate rules. How does that work for a weekly slot?
faqs.answer: Pre-clear the tutor once and the rest of the term is straightforward. Most Mumbai societies will register a recurring visitor for a fixed day and time when the resident requests it in advance, which avoids the tutor waiting at the gate while your paid hour runs down. We send you the tutor's name and identity details before the first visit so you can submit them to the committee or the gate app. In towers across Kandivali, Chembur, Powai and Thane this is routine. Tell us at the enquiry stage if your society needs paperwork, because it affects which evening we schedule.

faqs.question: Does online tuition work for a student struggling with Extended content?
faqs.answer: It works well for teaching the missing content and less well for the diagnosis. Watching a student attack an unfamiliar Extended question in person tells a tutor where the thinking actually breaks, which a shared screen tends to hide. Our usual approach is a home diagnostic followed by online sessions once the tutor knows the student, especially for families in Kasarvadavali, Panvel or Dahisar where travel would otherwise kill the weekly slot inside a month. Online also makes three short sessions a week possible before an entry deadline, which a travelling tutor cannot offer at any price.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out?
faqs.answer: Tell us after the second session and we will replace them. Fit is the one thing we cannot verify in advance, and a tier case in particular needs a tutor the student will admit confusion to rather than perform for. The diagnostic notes and the marked papers transfer to the replacement, so you are not paying for the same first hour twice. There is no argument and no retention conversation. The common reasons are pace and manner rather than competence, and it is far better to say it in week two than to lose six weeks of a window that does not reopen.

faqs.question: What should we realistically see after four weeks?
faqs.answer: A clear written opinion on the tier, backed by marks rather than impressions. By week four a tutor should have run a diagnostic, taught two or three of the topics the Core route leaves out, re-tested them cold, and told you whether the gap is content, speed or confidence. The grade itself will not have moved much, and anyone claiming it has is reading noise in a small sample. If nobody has committed to an opinion by then, raise it directly. The window to influence the school's entry decision is finite, and four weeks is a meaningful part of it.

You will get two or three profiles of tutors who have taught both tiers of that subject and who already travel your side of the city. You speak to them yourself, pick one, and the first session is a diagnostic rather than a lesson. Finding an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai before the entry deadline is the part still in your hands.

sections.heading: How IB Gram builds a shortlist of IGCSE tutors in Mumbai
paragraphs: The enquiry that reaches a coordinator is almost always plural. A mother in Khar West writes that her daughter is in Year 10 with nine subjects and four of them are a problem. A father in Chembur asks for help with everything except Art and Design. The first job is to argue the list down, because a single all IB and IGCSE subjects tutor in Mumbai does not exist, and a household running four separate people through the week has bought a timetable problem rather than solved a grade problem.

So the intake is deliberately specific. We ask for the subject list exactly as the school entered it, including which sciences are taken separately and which are combined, the last two report cards with the teacher comments and not only the grades, one piece of marked work from each weak subject, and one sentence about what the student wants after Year 11. That last item reorders the shortlist more often than the grades do. A student aiming at Higher Level (HL) Physics in the Diploma Programme (DP) has a different emergency from one aiming at a Business and Economics pathway at A Level, even when both report cards look identical.

Only then do profiles go out. Each shortlisted tutor is attached to one subject and to the papers inside it rather than to a board in general, and the profile states which syllabus components that person has taught and across how many exam cycles. A family in Thane hiring for Mathematics and Chemistry will normally see two different people with two different availabilities. Where the honest answer is one subject now and the second after the December mocks, the coordinator says so in writing before anyone is asked to commit to a standing weekly home tuition slot.
The plan that goes back to the parent names the subjects we are not tutoring and gives a reason for each one. Most parents tell us afterwards that this was the more useful half of the document.

2. A coordinator names the two or three subjects where paid help changes a grade.

sections.heading: Eight to ten subjects, six in the Diploma: the load a Mumbai fifteen-year-old carries
paragraphs: Most IGCSE students in Mumbai enter eight to ten subjects. A common set runs English First Language or English as a Second Language, English Literature, Mathematics, either three separate sciences or Coordinated Sciences, a second language such as French, Spanish, Hindi or Marathi, a humanity such as History, Geography or Global Perspectives, and one or two options drawn from Economics, Business Studies, Computer Science, Art and Design, Drama, Music or Physical Education. The compulsory core sits in every timetable; the options move with the school's block structure, which is why two students in the same class can have completely different weeks.

Set that against the Diploma Programme (DP), where a student takes six subjects, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), alongside Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and the creativity, activity and service strand. The DP is heavier per subject and much narrower. IGCSE is the opposite shape: nearly twice as many subjects, each with its own teacher, its own two to four papers, its own command words, its own practical or coursework component in several cases, and its own internal deadline that the school sets and moderates.

The breadth is what makes the programme survivable and also what makes it unfixable by brute force. No single subject is heavy enough to collapse a week, so nothing feels urgent until a mock paper says otherwise. At the same time, eight shallow fronts mean no subject reliably gets the twenty uninterrupted minutes a day that moves a grade. Parents often read a mediocre report card as eight small problems and go shopping for eight small solutions. It is almost never eight problems.

Whether a paper is sat at the Core or Extended tier, and whether the school runs Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, changes the paper numbers and the available grade range rather than the arithmetic of the week; those are conversations to have with the subject teacher before hiring anyone. No agency can honestly sell all IB and IGCSE subjects as home classes Mumbai families book one evening a week, and a provider that offers exactly that is describing a billing model rather than a teaching plan.
bullets: Eight to ten subjects at IGCSE against six in the Diploma Programme
Each subject carries its own papers, command words and internal deadlines
Core subjects are fixed; option blocks differ student by student
Core or Extended tiering changes paper numbers, not the weekly arithmetic
A bad report card is usually fewer problems than it has subjects

sections.heading: Which two or three subjects actually warrant paid help?
paragraphs: Three tests decide it. Does the grade matter for what the student does after Year 11, is one small gap dragging several topics at once, and is the school's own support in that subject genuinely thin? A subject that fails all three rarely justifies a paid tutor, whatever the report card looks like. A subject that passes two of them usually needs help before the next assessment cycle rather than after it.

This is why the lowest mark is so often the wrong subject to buy. A weak grade in an option that will be dropped at the end of Year 11, in a subject nobody downstream will ever ask about, costs very little. A middling grade in Mathematics costs a great deal if the student intends to take HL Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, because the school will look at exactly that grade when it builds Diploma sets. The same logic applies to Physics and Chemistry for a student heading towards engineering or medicine, and to English for anyone whose written answers carry marks in four other subjects.

The second test matters more than parents expect. One weak algebra foundation shows up as a Mathematics problem, a Physics problem and a Chemistry calculations problem on the same report card, and an IGCSE private tutor Mumbai parents hire for Chemistry alone will spend half of every session repairing algebra anyway. Fix the gap at its source and three grades move. The same is true of extended writing: a student who cannot structure a six-mark answer loses marks in Biology, History, Business Studies and Geography simultaneously. Those are single purchases with multiple returns, and they are the best value on the list.

Subject by subject, the return on tutoring is uneven at this level. Mathematics, Additional Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry reward it most, because the gap is usually technique on structured questions and that is teachable in weeks. Economics, Business Studies and Computer Science reward it where the problem is command words, data response or pseudocode rather than content. Art and Design, Drama, Music performance, Physical Education and the Global Perspectives team project reward it least: the work is produced and assessed inside the school, studio and rehearsal hours are the real input, and an outside home tutor can advise on planning but must not touch the submission.
bullets: Buy the subject whose grade a future course actually requires
Buy the gap that is dragging three subjects, not one weak mark
Algebra and extended writing are the two highest-return repairs at IGCSE
Leave coursework-assessed and performance subjects to the school department
Motivation problems do not respond to a second teacher in the room

sections.heading: Where IGCSE home tutors cluster across Mumbai's six zones
paragraphs: South Mumbai runs from Colaba and Cuffe Parade through Churchgate, Fort, Peddar Road, Walkeshwar, Breach Candy, Tardeo and Worli. Supply here is deepest in English, Economics, Business Studies and Mathematics, and thinnest in Additional Mathematics and Computer Science, which is where island families most often end up taking one subject on screen. Distances are short and the clock is not: a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba can lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals at seven in the evening, so matching stays inside the island rather than pulling someone down the Coastal Road from Bandra.

The Western Suburbs stretch from Bandra and Khar West through Santacruz, Juhu, Andheri, Goregaon East, Malad, Kandivali East, Borivali and Dahisar East, and hold the largest pool of IGCSE subject specialists in the city, including the science teachers other zones borrow. Match along the Western Line rather than across it. Khar to Santacruz or Malad to Kandivali East holds for a full term; Bandra to Dahisar East at six in the evening does not, even with Metro Lines 2A and 7 running above the Western Express Highway and Link Road. Most IGCSE tutors near me Mumbai searches come from exactly this corridor, and they are the easiest to fill.

The Central Suburbs cover Powai, Chandivali, Ghatkopar and Kurla, with Metro Line 1 and the Santacruz-Chembur Link Road doing the work the Central Line cannot. Powai is the anomaly: physically central, with no station of its own, reached by road from Andheri East along JVLR or from Kanjurmarg and Ghatkopar. Supply around Hiranandani Gardens and Chandivali is strong in Mathematics, Physics and Computer Science and noticeably thinner in second languages. The Eastern Suburbs, from Chembur and Govandi up through Vikhroli and Bhandup to Mulund, carry fewer IGCSE specialists per locality, though the Eastern Freeway puts a Chembur tutor into South Mumbai faster than the map suggests, and the Harbour Line and Monorail cover the rest.

Navi Mumbai is planned in nodes, so Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short run from the next along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway, and tutors are matched node to node. The Atal Setu has changed weekend travel from the island city, but a weekday evening crossing still rarely survives a full term. Thane spreads from the station across Pokhran Road, Majiwada, Hiranandani Estate and the length of Ghodbunder Road, where a tutor near the station reaches Kasarvadavali in twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour in the evening. Families comparing IGCSE home tutors in Mumbai across zones should assume the tutor lives inside the zone, because the ones who do not will quietly renegotiate the slot by the second month.

sections.heading: How the IGCSE year lands on the Mumbai school calendar
paragraphs: Families here sit the IGCSE at schools whose calendars run from June to the following March or April: Cathedral and John Connon School in Fort, B.D. Somani International School in Cuffe Parade, Bombay International School at Babulnath, Activity High School on Peddar Road, Aditya Birla World Academy in Tardeo, Jamnabai Narsee International School and Utpal Shanghvi Global School in Juhu, Hiranandani Foundation School in Powai, NES International School in Mulund West, Smt. Sulochanadevi Singhania School in Thane and D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of those schools, with Cambridge International Education or with Pearson Edexcel; the calendars simply set the pressure points every family in Mumbai, Maharashtra works around.

June and July are the quiet months and the ones parents waste. A Year 10 student has just picked an option block and a Year 11 student has just understood how little of Year 10 stayed. This is the only stretch of the year when adding help in one subject costs nothing in sleep. By late August the first unit tests land, coursework briefs are issued in Art and Design, Computer Science and the sciences, and the student who is behind in two subjects begins to be behind in four because the written work piles onto the revision.

October brings the Diwali break, which families consistently overfill. Three subjects crammed into a two-week holiday produces a tired student and no retained method. November and December are the mocks, and they are the single most informative event of the two years, because mock papers are the first time most students see the real paper structure and timing. A home tutor brought in during January is working with evidence; one brought in during September is working with a parent's hunch.

January and February carry the coursework and practical deadlines and the point at which entries are finalised, so the subject set stops being negotiable. March to May is exam technique only, with the monsoon still months away but the traffic no kinder. The last six weeks are for tapering: no new tutor, no new subject, no new method. Anything introduced that late competes with revision the student has already planned.
bullets: June and July: the cheapest window to add one subject
Late August: unit tests plus coursework briefs land together
November and December mocks give the first real evidence of paper technique

sections.heading: Is home tuition or online better when a student needs help in three subjects?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the lead option and the right default for the first subject. A tutor at the dining table sees the file, the half-finished past paper, the phone face-up next to the calculator and the way the student actually works, and none of that survives a screen. IGCSE home tuition in Mumbai also removes the student's travel, which is the whole argument in a city where getting to a centre in Andheri from Goregaon East in the evening costs more time than the lesson itself.

The multi-subject case is where the honest trade-off shows up. Two home tutors a week is manageable in most households. Three is where it breaks, because each visit carries its own gate entry, its own arrival drift and its own reshuffled dinner, and the student loses the free evening that the help was supposed to protect. The common arrangement that survives a full term across Mumbai is one home tutor for the structural subject, usually Mathematics or written English, and a second subject taught online. An IGCSE online tutor in Mumbai also solves scarcity: Additional Mathematics, Computer Science and some second languages simply do not have a local specialist in every zone, and a Kharghar or Mulund family will wait months for one who does not exist.

Hybrid is the arrangement we recommend most often for Year 11. The subject meets in person once a week for the teaching, then runs a short screen session before an assessment to mark a timed paper together. It keeps the travel count at one and still gives the student contact at the point where it matters. For students in Navi Mumbai and on Ghodbunder Road the hybrid pattern is frequently the only version that holds through the monsoon.

What we will not do is sell a single home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai parents sometimes ask for. One person teaching Physics, French and Business Studies to the same student is strong in one of them, and the parent pays the same rate for all three.
bullets: Home tuition first: the tutor sees the file and the working habits
Two home visits a week is workable; three usually collapses the evenings
Online solves scarcity in Additional Mathematics, Computer Science and second languages
Hybrid keeps one visit and adds a screen session before assessments
One tutor for every subject means one subject taught well and the rest guessed

sections.heading: What we check before an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai reaches your building
paragraphs: Every tutor on the platform clears identity verification, has their qualifications checked against the documents rather than the claim, and gives a teaching history that names the board, the subject, the specific papers and the exam cycles they have taught. A reference call follows for anyone who has taught at a school. The subject screen is separate for every subject a tutor is listed under, which is deliberate: a strong Physics teacher is not automatically a Chemistry teacher, and nothing about an IGCSE home tutor in Mumbai being excellent at one subject tells you anything about the second one on their profile.

That matters more on a multi-subject enquiry than anywhere else, because breadth is exactly where unverified tutors oversell. A profile claiming all the sciences plus Mathematics plus Economics at this level is the warning sign, not the convenience it looks like. When a family needs two subjects, we would rather send two people and say so than send one and let the second subject quietly become homework supervision at a teaching rate.

Parents should run their own checks in the first session, and they take ten minutes. Ask the tutor to name the papers in that subject and what each one tests. Ask what the command words mean in practice and how a six-mark answer differs from a four-mark one. Ask them to mark one piece of the student's recent work in front of you and explain where the marks were lost. A tutor who has taught the syllabus answers all three without preparation. One who has not will talk about concepts in general terms and avoid the paper.

The building side is practical. Societies across Mumbai run visitor registers, app-based gate passes or a phone call to the flat, and a tutor who is turned away twice stops being reliable. Clear a standing weekly entry with your society office in the first week, share the tutor's name and phone number with the gate, and keep the sessions in a room with a door and a table rather than a bedroom.

A separate subject screen for every subject a tutor is listed under

sections.heading: The subject nobody is watching, and how to triage a report card that is bad everywhere
paragraphs: In almost every multi-subject enquiry there is one subject nobody has mentioned. The marks are unremarkable rather than alarming, the teacher comment says the student is capable of more, and the student never brings it up. That is usually the subject in real trouble, because the others are failing loudly enough to be managed. Three questions find it. Can the student name the papers in that subject? Is there any marked work in the file from the last two months? Has every mark so far come from the same kind of assessment, typically recall tests, with no structured or extended questions yet? If the answer to all three is no, the grade has not been tested yet and the mock will do it.

A report card that is weak across all eight or nine subjects is a different animal and almost never eight separate subject problems. It is one working-habits problem wearing eight costumes: no revision method beyond rereading, no system for notes, homework submitted but not checked, late nights, and a phone in the room during every study hour. It can also be a transfer effect. A student who moved into Year 9 from a CBSE or ICSE school in Mumbai knows the content and has never been asked to write an IGCSE structured answer, and that shows up as a uniform drop in exactly the way a knowledge gap does not.

The treatment for the across-the-board case is one tutor, not eight, and the right one is the highest-leverage subject taught by somebody who will also rebuild method: retrieval practice, timed questions from the start, a weekly plan the student writes themselves. If the pattern repeats after a term of genuine effort, a screening conversation with the school counsellor about reading speed, processing or attention is worth more than a second IGCSE tutor Mumbai agencies will happily supply.

Sequencing across the two years is the last piece. Year 9 is for the subject set and for fixing whichever of algebra or written English is weaker, because both compound. Year 10 runs one subject, the structural one. The December mocks in Year 11 decide the second, and a third is justified only as a short six to eight week block of exam technique, never as another standing commitment. Running three from the start of Year 10 leaves a family with nothing to add when it actually matters, and a student who has forgotten how to study alone.

sections.heading: What does progress look like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle?
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see a change in method, not in marks. The student attempts a structured question before asking for help, writes something in the margin of a past paper, and can say what a command word is asking for. Marks move later and they move unevenly. Anyone promising a grade jump in a month is selling something, and IB Gram does not guarantee grades, at IGCSE or anywhere else. What a good tutor controls is the quality and volume of the right practice; the student controls whether it happens on the other six days.

At one term the measure is the specific paper type the tutoring targeted. If the work was structured six-mark answers in Biology, the Biology structured questions should improve while the multiple-choice paper stays where it was. That narrowness is a feature. It tells you the help is working on something real rather than producing a general feeling of improvement that evaporates in the mock.

At one exam cycle, which for most Mumbai families means the mocks and then the May series, the grade is the measure, and so is what happened in the untutored subjects. This is the number parents forget to look at. Two subjects tutored properly should lift those two grades without the other seven sliding, and if the other seven slid, the week was overloaded and the plan was wrong even though the tutoring worked.

Honest limits apply. A tutor cannot fix a subject the student has decided to resent, cannot make a coursework deadline that passed in January come back, and cannot compress two years of missing foundation into the six weeks before a paper. Where that is the situation, we say it at the shortlist stage. A family in Vashi or Borivali deciding to hire one home tutor instead of three, after a conversation that talked them out of two, is a better outcome for us than three billable slots that collapse in week five.

sections.heading: How should a two-year plan start, and what does the first session cover?
paragraphs: Start by sending four things: the subject list exactly as the school entered it with tiers marked, the last two report cards including the comments, one piece of marked work from each subject you are worried about, and one line about what the student wants to do after Year 11. A coordinator comes back with a shortlist for two subjects at most, and with reasoning for every subject left off it. If you disagree with the exclusions, say so; the argument itself usually surfaces the information the report card hid.

The first session is diagnostic and should feel like it. The tutor works through recent marked work and a short piece of timed writing from the syllabus rather than teaching a topic, and finishes by naming the two things costing the most marks right now. Expect a specific answer such as rearranging equations before substituting, or answering only the first half of a two-part question. Expect it in writing within a day or two.

After that the standing slot begins, at a fixed time the household can actually hold for a term. A Year 10 plan usually means one subject running through the year, a review after the December mocks in Year 11, and a decision then about whether a second subject or a short block of exam technique is worth the evening it costs. Some families never add the second. That is frequently the right call, and nobody at IB Gram will push a household into a third weekly visit that the student's week cannot absorb.

If the match is wrong, say so after two sessions rather than two months. We replace the tutor and keep the plan, because the plan was built on the student's papers and not on the person delivering it.

faqs.question: How many subjects should my child have a tutor for at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Two is the realistic maximum for most households, and one is often better in Year 10. A student taking nine subjects already has nine teachers, nine sets of homework and nine deadlines, so every tutor you add removes an evening of independent practice, which is where IGCSE marks are actually earned. Pick the subject whose grade a future course requires, or the gap that is dragging several subjects at once. A third subject is defensible only as a short block of exam technique between the mocks and the final papers, not as another standing weekly commitment.

faqs.question: My daughter's lowest mark is in Art and Design. Should that be the subject we tutor?
faqs.answer: Probably not. Art and Design is assessed on work produced and moderated inside the school, so studio hours with her own teacher are the input that counts, and an outside tutor can discuss planning but must not touch the submission. Ask two questions instead: does any course after Year 11 require that grade, and is the weakness costing marks anywhere else? If the answer to both is no, a low mark in one option subject is a cheap mark to lose. The same money spent on Mathematics or on structuring written answers usually moves three grades rather than one.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all of my son's subjects?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer to do so is a reason to be careful rather than relieved. IGCSE subjects each have their own papers, command words and mark schemes, and the person who genuinely teaches Physics to Extended level is not the same person who teaches French writing or Business Studies data response. One tutor across six subjects means one subject taught well and the rest supervised at a teaching rate. Where a student needs help in several areas, we match separate specialists per subject, sequence them so only one or two run at a time, and tell you plainly which subjects need nobody.

faqs.question: The report card is weak in every subject. Do we need eight tutors?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not. A report card that is uniformly weak is usually one working-habits problem rather than eight subject problems: no revision method beyond rereading, notes that are never used, homework submitted but never checked, and late nights. It can also be a transfer effect in students who moved into Year 9 from a CBSE or ICSE school and have never written an IGCSE structured answer. Start with one tutor in the highest-leverage subject who will also rebuild method, give it a term, and involve the school counsellor if the same pattern repeats despite genuine effort.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects benefit least from private tutoring?
faqs.answer: The ones whose marks are produced inside the school. Art and Design, Drama, Music performance, Physical Education and the Global Perspectives team project are built from studio time, rehearsal, practical sessions and group work that a tutor cannot replicate or submit. Coursework components in any subject fall into the same category: a tutor may discuss method and planning, but the work must be the student's own and the school moderates it. Tutoring returns most on Mathematics, Additional Mathematics, Physics and Chemistry, and on the exam technique in Economics, Business Studies and Computer Science, where the gap is usually structure rather than knowledge.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to our building in Kharghar on a weekday evening?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the tutor is matched inside Navi Mumbai. Kharghar works well with tutors based in Belapur, Nerul, Vashi or Panvel, because the nodes connect along Palm Beach Road and the Sion-Panvel Highway and the run takes minutes rather than an hour. What does not hold is a tutor pulled across from the island city or the Western Suburbs for a 7pm slot; the Atal Setu has improved that crossing, but weekday evening traffic still makes it the first arrangement to break. Ask where your tutor lives before you agree the slot, not afterwards.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during a home tuition session?
faqs.answer: Not for the whole session, but somebody should be in the flat. Most families keep the lesson in a living or dining area with the door open, which suits a fifteen-year-old better than a bedroom and removes any awkwardness for the tutor as well. Be present for the first session so you hear the diagnosis directly, then drop in for the last five minutes of later sessions to hear what was covered and what was set. That five minutes is the single most useful habit parents adopt, because it keeps the work between sessions visible to you.

faqs.question: We live off Ghodbunder Road in Thane. How do we schedule two tutors in one evening week?
faqs.answer: Put both sessions on days the tutor can reach you before the Ghodbunder Road evening build-up, and never on the same evening. A tutor living near Thane station reaches Kasarvadavali in about twenty minutes off-peak and close to an hour at peak, so a 6pm start and a 7.30pm start on the same day will not both happen. Spread them across the week, keep one of the two online if the specialist is not local to Thane, and agree a fixed fallback day in advance for the sessions the monsoon will inevitably move.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition fees in Mumbai depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and we do not publish a price list because the honest answer varies by request. Fees depend on the board and tier, the level of the subject, how scarce that subject specialist is in your zone, the travel the tutor absorbs to reach your building, and the session length and frequency you agree. Additional Mathematics or Computer Science in a zone with few specialists costs more than English in the Western Suburbs. Online sessions remove the travel component. Ask for the rate per session and the expected number of sessions per month before you commit, so you are comparing the same thing across tutors.

faqs.question: How do we find the best IGCSE tutor in Mumbai for Additional Mathematics?
faqs.answer: Stop looking for the best one and look for the right one, because the title means nothing and the fit is measurable. For Additional Mathematics specifically, ask which syllabus components the tutor has taught, how many exam cycles they have taken a cohort through, and how they handle the step up from the core Mathematics paper. Then ask them to mark one of your child's recent answers in front of you. The specialists for this subject are concentrated in the Western and Central Suburbs, around Powai, Chandivali and Andheri, so families in South Mumbai or Panvel often take it online.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after a month?
faqs.answer: Tell us after two sessions rather than at the end of the month, and we replace the tutor while keeping the plan. The plan was built on your child's marked work and subject priorities, not on the individual delivering it, so a replacement starts from the same diagnosis rather than from scratch. Say specifically what is wrong: sessions running as homework supervision, no written summary, poor timekeeping, or a style the student cannot work with. A month of polite silence costs a term, and in Year 11 there is no spare term available.

faqs.question: My son is in Year 9. Is it too early to bring in an IGCSE tutor?
faqs.answer: Year 9 is the best time for exactly one thing: fixing whichever of algebra or written English is weaker. Both compound into the subjects he will sit in Years 10 and 11, and both are far cheaper to repair now than in the term before the papers. What Year 9 is not for is a tutor in every subject he finds hard, because subject sets are still settling and he may drop two of them. Use the year to repair foundations and to choose the option block well, then add subject help once Year 10 assessments show where the real gaps are.

sections.heading: Which programme is your child actually in, and what changes for a tutor?
paragraphs: Families in Jogeshwari are usually choosing between two systems that look similar from outside the school gate and behave very differently inside it. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs as a continuum: the Primary Years Programme (PYP) in the early years, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) through the middle school, and the Diploma Programme (DP) in the final two years. Cambridge International Education runs IGCSE in Years 9 to 11 and then usually hands students to AS and A Level or to the DP. Pearson Edexcel runs a parallel International GCSE used by a smaller number of schools in Mumbai. A tutor has to know which of these your child sits in before they open a book, because the same topic is assessed in three different ways across them.

PYP tuition is rarely about content. There is no external examination and no prescribed syllabus of facts, so a PYP home tutor in the Western Suburbs is working on reading fluency, number sense, written expression and the habit of explaining reasoning out loud. Parents sometimes arrive asking for worksheets and leave understanding that the useful work is building the base that MYP will test. MYP is where the shape changes: every subject group is marked against published criteria, each criterion is described in strands, and a student can know the content and still score poorly because they answered the question instead of meeting the criterion.

The Diploma Programme adds the part that catches most Jogeshwari families off guard. Six subjects, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), plus the core: Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment (IA) that is marked by the school and moderated by the IB. The IA calendar, not the examination calendar, is what makes DP1 and DP2 difficult, and a home tutor who only teaches content will be useless in the fortnight when three drafts are due together.

IGCSE has its own structural decision that parents often do not know they are making. Many subjects are tiered: Mathematics and the sciences run Core and Extended papers, and the grade ceiling on the Core tier is lower. A student placed on Core in Year 9 because of a shaky start can be stuck below the grade an IB Diploma place needs two years later. This is one of the most common reasons an IGCSE home tutor is engaged in Jogeshwari, and it is worth raising with the school early rather than in Year 11.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, Core and Extended: what a tutor has to get right
paragraphs: Because this page covers all IB and IGCSE subjects, the first job of a good match is not teaching, it is diagnosis. A parent asks for English help; the useful question is whether the child is in Cambridge IGCSE First Language English, IGCSE English as a Second Language, DP Language A Literature or DP Language A Language and Literature, because the four demand different skills and reward different habits. Get this wrong and you pay for twelve weeks of competent teaching aimed at the wrong examination. We ask for the subject code or a photograph of the report card before matching, and it saves more trouble than any other single step.

A worked example makes the point. Take Cambridge IGCSE First Language English, syllabus 0500, Paper 2. Question 1 is directed writing: the student reads a passage and writes in a specified form for a specified audience, say a speech or a letter, and the mark scheme splits credit between reading the source properly and the quality of the writing itself. Students who lose marks here almost never lose them on vocabulary. They lose them because they wrote a good essay that ignored half the source, or because they used the source well and forgot the form. A tutor who knows the paper teaches the student to annotate the passage for the two or three ideas the question actually asks them to develop, then to build the response around those, then to check the register matches the stated audience. Two sessions of that is often worth more than a term of general comprehension work.

Now put the same child in DP Language A Language and Literature Paper 1, guided textual analysis. The text is unseen and non-literary, there is a guiding question, and the examiner wants a focused analysis of how the text constructs meaning, not a summary and not a list of devices. The reading skill transfers from IGCSE; the structure does not. A tutor who taught the 0500 approach unchanged into DP1 will produce a student who writes neatly and scores in the middle band. This is exactly why we match on board and level, not on subject name alone, and why the shortlist shows which syllabus a tutor has actually taught.

The same logic runs across the other groups. IB Mathematics splits into Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation, each at HL and SL, and moving between them mid-course is painful. The DP sciences all carry a scientific investigation assessed on published criteria rather than on getting the expected result. Individuals and Societies subjects carry written internal assessments with strict word limits and a required structure. Covering all IB and IGCSE subjects through one tutor in Jogeshwari is rarely the honest answer, and booking through one platform instead means we can place a second specialist for the second subject rather than pretending one person covers everything well.
